Senses.Explanation: By what is it verified? Xutang Zhiyu, inaugurating the Xingsheng temple — great mechanism, round response, the way without directions, troops following the seal, generals the tally, the phoenix come to rite and the qilin to omen, the ancestor-intent of the west achieved — still asks: after all, by what is it verified? and answers with a long silence, one breath wordless yet holding the images. Tiantong Rujing, when the great stone drum arrives — the lone blind eye at the crown of the head, the great man's great seeing tipping over the sky inside the jar, the great entering the small and the myriad transformations bestowed on all — asks it and answers with the oriole tuning a new tongue on the tall tree and the plum breathing old fragrance from an old branch. Foguo Weibai, on New Year's Day, crosses out last year and this year, new Chan and old Chan, with one stroke of the stick — all annulled at once, and made complete — then asks, knocks once, and lets the auspicious wind of the six directions rise and the harmony of ten thousand regions flow. Duanqiao Miaolun, returning to enter the temple, points at the three gates: the years he left through this door every step trod on it, today entering every meeting collides with it — after all by what is it verified? — and answers by looking up at the temple plaque: bound to be said. Shixi Xinyue, at the dowager-empress's birthday hall, gathers all the auspiciousness into the moment before King Glorious Silence, beyond the empty kalpa, before news omens anything and the true body is fully displayed — then asks, and the ninth heaven's auspicious air coils at dawn while the four seas together behold her who models motherhood. Miyun Yuanwu, mourning that no one raises the old cases anymore and that only this kind of man can shoulder this kind of affair, grants that there happens to be a proof-place — by what verified? — and claps his raised hands: beat the drum, everyone look. Feiyin Tongrong, at the shrine-hall station of his entry, names the guardian its hedge and the dharma its golden moat, charged at Vulture Peak and unforgotten to this day — and by what verified? watch this one petal of incense burn. Pufu Zhuo, in instruction, orders each trainee to take the life-cutting knife and sever the life-root at one stroke before the beginningless kalpa, killing buddha, ancestor and demon until finished — the least fiber and a film grows over the eye — after all by what is it verified? Guanyin bodhisattva spends cash on a hu-bing, puts down her hand, and it is a steamed bun.

Senses.PreferredTarget: Take great perfect awakening as my monastery
SearchAliases: take great perfect awakening as my monastery
Senses.Note: The line makes great perfect awakening the monastic dwelling. Wuzhun answers it with an image of a lame horse tied to a dead stake; Dahui contrasts the usual summer-retreat formula with his own assembly’s impossible fare. Beijian says that treating the line as a fixed site digs a pit in level ground. Po’an extends the summer gathering to grasses and trees across the world. Shixi warns later learners against getting caught in it, and Chushi asks what equal wisdom leaves of sacred and ordinary rank. The dwelling becomes an active question at each retreat.

Occurrences.Kwic: 君與舊歲君兩人聞恁麼告報，冷地不甘，却向佛殿角頭互相耳語。且道說箇什麼？一年好處君須記，三月江南啼鷓鴣。結夏，小參。肉臭來蠅，垛生招箭，擬要完全，却成兩片。所以，從門入者不是家珍，流出𮌎中亦須吐却。靈利漢不受人瞞，向這裏擔得一片版去，我當刎頸而謝。若據見前一眾，也有靈利不受人瞞底。有則有，敢問西天那蘭陀寺今日有幾人結制？若也知得，非惟不受人瞞，便見此土西天絲毫無間；若也不知，清凉分明道破，也要諸人共委。乃云：前三百，後五百。解夏，小參。以大圓覺為我伽藍，癩馬繫枯樁；身心安居平等性智，黑牛臥死水。更說休夏自恣，取驗蠟人，大似白日青天，大開眼了說夢。不見道：家無白澤之圖，必無如是妖怪。所以，衲僧家尋常蹉口道著佛字，便須漱口三年；不覺聞正因二字，急急臨流洗耳。是故，山僧一夏九十日與諸人同行、同坐、同起、同臥，直是頂戴諸人，不敢錯悞諸人一絲頭子。分明恁麼道，也是久日樺來唇。冬夜，小參。正令全提，十方坐斷，放開一線，滿路歌謠，便見東家走過西家、西家走過東家，合掌擎拳，互相慶賀，道：且喜一陽來復

Occurrences.Kwic: 是，千處百處非而亦是；一處非，千處百處是而亦非；是而亦非，非而亦是。此兩句語以那句為主？拍禪床，云：是非裏薦取。上堂：古德道，暫時不在，如同死人。且道不在却在什麼處？喝！大好不在。掩室和尚忌燒香。甌峰布鐵連陣，我曾長袖拂開；甌峰擲金剛圈，我曾鐵鞭擊碎。沒仇讎處起仇讎，無怨對中作怨對。今日何以報之？插香，云：報之以此為最。上堂：露柱燈籠，為諸人說底是第二句。國師良久：是第二句。真實第一句作麼生？擬將心意學玄宗，大似西行却向東。結夏，上堂。以大圓覺為我伽藍，過去諸佛罪不重科，見在菩薩理無曲斷，未來學人咄切忌草裏輥。上堂，舉：趙州訪一菴主，問云：有麼？有麼？主竪起拳頭，州云：水淺不是泊船處。又訪一菴主，問云：有麼？有麼？主亦竪起拳頭，州云：能縱能奪，能殺能活。遂禮拜。師云：能縱能奪，能殺能活，也是慣得其便。上堂。喝一喝，云：者裏不許鑽龜打瓦。便下座。上堂：機先轉步，句下騰身。與夫睡來合眼，󰕖來開口底，相去幾何？莫有善窺鞭影者麼？上堂。直下猶難會，尋言轉更賒。拈主丈，云：不得喚者箇作主丈子。

Senses.Explanation: A scriptural retreat line turns the monastery into a question of where and how one dwells. Wuzhun and Dahui resist taking the formula as an easy retreat plan; Beijian calls settling on it a pit in level ground. Po’an opens the dwelling across the world; Shixi warns later learners against getting stuck; Chushi tests the equal wisdom it implies.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Feiyin: At the opening of the winter retreat, a monk asks Feiyin Tongrong about the proper business of establishing the rules. Feiyin first tells him to sit, then strikes him when he tries to reply. Addressing the assembly, Feiyin says his monastery will not follow an old routine of achievement and introduces the inherited vow with 'therefore it is said.' He then plays with releasing, gathering, and neither releasing nor gathering, pressing the monks to respond directly. The quoted 'my monastery' is the model retreat practitioner's first-person vow taught in the Perfect Awakening Sutra; the blow and the present challenge are Feiyin's.

Occurrences.Kwic: 裏，得到清平有幾人？除夜，小參。舊歲今宵去，去去實不去；新年明日來，來來實不來。萬古長空無變異，循環日月空相催。山僧與麼告報，眾中或有不甘底出來道：大小育王話作兩橛。又作麼生祇遣？雖然如是，也須真箇始得。今時師僧往往語言相似、州縣不同，所以差之毫釐、失之千里。卓拄杖一下，云：誰識閻羅王是鬼？結夏，小參。若據正令提綱，直須寶幢路上荒草連天、玉几峯前荊榛滿地，猶未為分外，而況三百、五百聚頭接耳，浩浩商量也大屈哉？育王今夜事不獲已，略借古人方便一路，與諸人赴箇程限。良久，以大圓覺為我伽藍，身心安居，平等性智，非不非、是不是，虎咬大虫、蛇吞鱉鼻。雖然，要且不得動著，動著則打折你驢𦝫。除夜，小參。無入作處，可煞見成；恰相當時，全沒巴鼻。鷲嶺妄傳迦葉，少林謾付神光，自餘列派分燈，未免󳯝相屈辱。只如今臘月三十日，一箇箇豈不知是歲除夜？更來這裏握節當𮌎，側聽箇什麼？山僧從而不識好惡，更向諸人面前分拏劈裂，也太無端。何故？彼此出家兒。解制，小參。以大圓覺為我伽藍，身心安居平等性智，所謂從四月十五日結也如是、至七月十五日解也如是、威音王已前亦如是、彌勒佛下生亦如是，萬年一念、一念萬年，無古、無今，不變、不異，便恁麼去，正坐在靈山窠臼中出頭不得。有般漢便道：衲僧家有甚固必？要行便行、要坐便坐，鉢盂裏屙屎、淨缾中吐唾，毀於佛、謗於法，不入眾數，熏修十不善因、成就五無間業。若恁麼去，又却墮在今時窠臼中，未有超脫一路。直饒恁麼、不恁麼，一時坐斷，別有生涯，點撿將來亦未可在。何故？又却墮在自己窠臼中轉身不得。如今要出靈山窠臼則易，要出今時窠臼則難；要出今時窠臼則易，要出自己窠臼則難。既然如是，且作麼生出得？拈拄杖，卓一下，云：靈山窠臼．今時窠臼．自己窠臼一擊粉碎了也。到這裏合作麼生？顧視左右，云：夜來何處火？燒出古人墳。結夏，小參。曹谿路上，無端浪起成堆；玉几峯前，誰信地平如掌？往復無間，動靜一源，伸出手觸著達磨大師眼睛，舉起步踏斷釋迦老子鼻孔，了無回避，逈絕安排，更說甚麼長期短期？只貴自家心肯意肯。既然如是，只如九十日中畢竟作麼生履踐？拄杖生根休用剪，鉢盂無柄不勞安。解夏，小參。機不離位，沉乎醉鄉；語不離窠，滯在金網。竪起拄杖，云：看，看！賓頭盧尊者現在山僧拄杖頭上，為諸人作自恣佛事，廣說一夏九十日內所得所證

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Wuzhun Shifan: In a short talk at the opening of the summer retreat, Wuzhun first invokes the inherited vow after saying he must borrow an old expedient for the gathered monks. The same selected passage also includes his short talk when the retreat ends. There he quotes the vow again and says that beginning, ending, and the time before either are alike. He then warns that even resting in the old sacred precedent, current freedom from rules, or one's own ability to cut through both becomes another rut. Wuzhun strikes the ground with his staff to break all three. The first-person words are the scripture's prescribed retreat vow; these tests and the staff action are Wuzhun's.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Jie’an Jin: During an instruction given while building a wall, Jie’an Jin quotes the prescribed retreat vow and says that if this is understood, guest and host can function without relying on a defensive wall or an office holder. He immediately turns the wall into an image of vulnerability: when insight is obscured, the six sense gates let thieves carry away one's treasure. Jie’an asks the assembly where its real master is, slaps his knee, and answers a possible objection. The first-person words are the scriptural model vow, not Jie’an's invention; the wall, thieves, and knee-slap are his teaching for this occasion.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Hansong Cao: At the opening of the summer retreat, a monk asks Hansong Zhicao to explain four difficult gates, and Hansong answers each in a clipped image. In the ensuing address, he quotes the inherited vow about making great awakening one's monastery and resting body and mind in equal wisdom. He then offers the assembly images of food from older Chan cases and says that direct recognition would open all the named gates; continued hesitation calls for practice while walking, sitting, morning, and evening. The vow is the scripture's prescribed speech for a retreat participant. Hansong supplies the replies, the challenge, and the closing question.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Jingtingsong: At the ceremony when Jingting Dezong takes a new abbot's seat, a monk asks how mind, Buddha, and things are to be denied, then presses for what lies beyond the three answers. Jingting replies with images and says he would cut off the questioner's tongue. In his following address he quotes the inherited retreat vow and says that understanding it here would make even impossible images such as piercing a weight intelligible; failing it leaves one exhausted only to see one's eyebrows before one's eyes. The first-person vow comes from the Perfect Awakening Sutra's model speech for an unspecified practitioner. The exchange and application are Jingting's.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Feiyin: At the opening of the winter retreat, a monk asks Feiyin Tongrong about the proper business of establishing the rules. Feiyin first tells him to sit, then strikes him when he tries to reply. Addressing the assembly, Feiyin says his monastery will not follow an old routine of achievement and introduces the inherited vow with 'therefore it is said.' He then plays with releasing, gathering, and neither releasing nor gathering, pressing the monks to respond directly. ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Wuzhun Shifan: In a short talk at the opening of the summer retreat, Wuzhun first invokes the inherited vow after saying he must borrow an old expedient for the gathered monks. The same selected passage also includes his short talk when the retreat ends. There he quotes the vow again and says that beginning, ending, and the time before either are alike. He then warns that even resting in the old sacred precedent, current freedom from rules, or one's own ability to cut through both becomes another rut. Wuzhun strikes the ground with his staff to break all three. The first-person words are the scripture's prescribed retreat vow; these tests and the staff action are Wuzhun's.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Hansong Cao: At the opening of the summer retreat, a monk asks Hansong Zhicao to explain four difficult gates, and Hansong answers each in a clipped image. In the ensuing address, he quotes the inherited vow about making great awakening one's monastery and resting body and mind in equal wisdom. He then offers the assembly images of food from older Chan cases and says that direct recognition would open all the named gates; continued hesitation calls for practice while walking, sitting, morning, and evening. The vow is the scripture's prescribed speech for a retreat participant. Hansong supplies the replies, the challenge, and the closing question.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Jingtingsong: At the ceremony when Jingting Dezong takes a new abbot's seat, a monk asks how mind, Buddha, and things are to be denied, then presses for what lies beyond the three answers. Jingting replies with images and says he would cut off the questioner's tongue. In his following address he quotes the inherited retreat vow and says that understanding it here would make even impossible images such as piercing a weight intelligible; failing it leaves one exhausted only to see one's eyebrows before one's eyes. The first-person vow comes from the Perfect Awakening Sutra's model speech for an unspecified practitioner. The exchange and application are Jingting's.

Senses.Explanation: The Perfect Awakening Sutra gives these first-person words as a model vow for an unspecified person entering a retreat: the practitioner is to take great awakening as 'my monastery' and let body and mind dwell in equal wisdom. The Buddha instructs the practitioner to say the vow; the quoted 'I' is not the Buddha describing his own residence. Feiyin uses it to challenge a monk at a winter retreat, Wuzhun uses it at the start and end of a summer retreat, Jie’an adopts its first-person wording while teaching about a wall and the sense gates, Hansong uses it while testing four gates, and Jingting cites it after an installation exchange.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The question frame (僧問) explicitly governs the exact graph-pair question, while the answer frame (師曰) begins Luohan Guichen’s response; all six rungs leave the questioning monk personally unnamed.

Senses.Explanation: Neither the ‘by-means-of’ graph (以) nor the ‘eight’ graph (八) is a paired character puzzle: the whole formula asks what graph the visible strokes make if they are not accepted as either familiar character. Chan records keep both halves together and answer through strokes, main text and commentary, or the entire canon. Liao'an uses the pair to open two hall addresses; Baichi asks a canon keeper which graph it is and calls the canon its phonetic gloss; and an unnamed monk puts the same full question to Luohan Guichen.

Senses.Explanation: Transmit mind by mind is a formula for direct dharma transmission, often coupled with not setting up written words. The Platform Sutra has Hongren give the formulation to Huineng, and Bodhidharma uses it in an answer to Huike. Xuefeng Yicun pairs it with Bodhidharma’s coming from the west, while Dahui Zonggao describes it as the formula used in place of verbal transmission. Mi’an Xianjie then criticizes treating it as a formula. The entry preserves both the transmission wording and that recorded criticism without adding a resolution.

Senses.Explanation: The phrase is a formal action cue: one staff strike punctuates an assertion, enthronement, or ritual transition and makes the preceding or following line present to the assembly. Feiyin Tongrong strikes after asking for the root meaning; Falun Wenyu strikes and shouts before calling both additions; Poshan Haiming strikes during a memorial address; Linwo Jian uses the strike when installing a new elder; Yunfeng closes a hall address with it; and Shiqi Tongyun strikes before leaving the seat. These are six named performances of the same visible action.

Senses.PreferredTarget: Cover it with this, leaving no corners exposed
SearchAliases: cover it with this, leaving no corners exposed
Senses.Note: After Huanyou Zhengchuan responds to Xiaoyan Debao’s staff challenge, Xiaoyan gives him a hat and says, “Cover it with this, leaving no corners exposed.” The gift has a plain use, but it also follows a test of whether the student can take up the teacher’s charge. Yinyuan’s collection preserves the exchange with a verse on carrying it forward. Zizhou asks whether one hat could conceal such a conspicuous figure. Dafang answers with a verse that links the hat to the earlier raised foot and shoe; Lingji writes of returning home after the body is laid bare. Each later poem reads the visible hat against what the encounter revealed.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J40/J40nB483.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zhufeng Min. Zhufeng uses the exact paired line in his own festival verse and repeats its question before extending it.

Senses.Explanation: "Alone in the wide span of heaven and earth, standing apart, how far can one gaze?" pairs an open setting with a solitary question. Named masters reuse the complete excerpt in their own hall talks, answers, and verses. Feiyin gives the line and then describes a solitary, unconfined stance; Tianan brings it into a birthday address. Yezhu uses the couplet as his answer about a visitor, and Lianfeng closes a hall talk with it after asking what must be borne. Zhufeng repeats the question at a festival address and extends it in his own verse.

Entries.SourceTerm: 日上無雲，麗天普照，眼中無翳，空裏無花

Senses.PreferredTarget: sun risen without clouds and shining throughout the sky, with no film in the eye and no flowers in empty space
SearchAliases: no film in the eye, no flowers in space
Senses.Note: The exact witnesses are parallel lamp recensions of one Linji address. One witness represents the exhausted family.

Occurrences.Kwic: 擬天下走，自起見障，以礙於心。日上無雲，麗天普照，眼中無翳，空裏無花。道流！儞欲得如法，但莫生疑，展則彌綸法界，収則絲髮不立，歷歷孤明，未曾欠少。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X78/X78n1553.xml). Tiansheng Expanded Lamp Record. The complete passage identifies Linji Yixuan as the speaker of the sentence containing the headword.

Senses.Explanation: Linji joins a cloudless sun and an unobstructed eye into one clarity image: nothing covers the sky, and no defect in the eye produces flowers in empty space. After warning that listeners raise their own obstructing views, Linji gives the four-clause line and tells them not to give rise to doubt.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T47/T47n1990.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Huiji of Yangshan, Yuanzhou. At summer's end, Weishan asks Yangshan Huiji what he has done below the mountain. Yangshan says he cleared a field and planted a measure of seed; Weishan says he has not wasted the summer. Yangshan returns the question, and Weishan answers with one midday meal and one sleep after nightfall. Yangshan grants that his teacher too has not wasted the summer, then sticks out his tongue. Weishan asks why he wounds his own life. Eating and sleeping answer work in the field, but the final challenge keeps their apparent equality open to examination. The line is a reply in this encounter, not a general diet or sleep prescription.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一則古人公案與諸人聽。昔仰山夏末上溈山省覲，溈云：『子一夏作甚麼？』仰云：『鋤得一片畬，種得一籮粟。』溈云：『子可謂不空過。』仰云：『和尚一夏作甚麼？』溈云：『日中一食，夜後一寢。』仰云：『和尚也可謂不空過。』道了乃吐舌。溈云：『寂子何得自傷己命？』大眾！溈仰父子主賓互換，縱奪可觀即且置，祇如仰山吐舌，溈山因甚道寂子自傷己命？若撿點得出
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J28/J28nB208.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Guxue Zhe. Guxue Zhenzhe raises the old exchange after defending a summer without sermons and his listeners' work carrying materials and gathering grain. Those who call it wasted because they have not acquired more religious explanations, he says, mistake what is fundamental. He then gives Weishan's meal-and-sleep answer beside Yangshan's farming. Rather than stop with their mutual praise, he asks why Weishan calls Yangshan's protruding tongue self-injury. Anyone who can examine that may count as a monk with nothing extra to do; otherwise, do not waste the present time. Ordinary work is defended, while the claim that nothing further is required is itself tested.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J37/J37nB392.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Hansong Cao. At the end of the retreat, Hansong Zhicao pairs clearing a field and sowing grain with a sea entered ever more deeply, then the midday meal and night's sleep with a mountain climbed ever higher. He imagines free movement and the capacity to act independently, even going beyond Buddha and patriarch. But if reputation and profit remain in mind and attachment to scenery persists, he changes register: clicking his teeth, he makes gestures of spraying water and drawing a talisman, ordering a rapid departure. The inherited line becomes his current contrast between deepening practice and a display still caught in attachments. The performance is not evidence that a literal spirit was expelled.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J39/J39nB441.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Tongzhen of Wanfeng. Wanfeng raises the abbreviated summer exchange through Yangshan's reply that Weishan too has not wasted the season. His verse says father and son each present their family manner, yet their same dream in different beds is difficult to express. Without summer's end and autumn's beginning, how would meeting and speaking become so intimate? The meal-and-sleep answer is therefore read through the personal and seasonal encounter, not as a detached minimum schedule for every practitioner. This version does not retain the tongue gesture and further rebuke, so those details should not be described as part of its quoted turn.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一聲堪著耳，又隨流水過前灘。復舉：溈山問仰山：寂子今夏在下面作何所務？仰山云：鋤得一片畬，下得一籮粟。溈山云：子今夏不空過。仰山却問云：和尚今夏作箇什麼？溈云：日中一食，夜後一寢。仰云：和尚今夏亦不空過。道了遂吐舌。溈云：寂子何得自傷己命？師拈云：仰山一夏不空過，脚露手穿；溈山不空過一夏，脚穿手露。古人則且止，只如淨慈一夏七顛八倒，是空
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X70/X70n1394.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Duanqiao Miaolun. Duanqiao Miaolun first describes retreat confinement as an iron hammer and release as roads open in every direction. He then raises Weishan and Yangshan's exchange, including the tongue gesture and rebuke. Yangshan's unwasted summer means exposed feet and worn hands, he says; Weishan's means worn feet and exposed hands. Having balanced them through that reversal, he asks whether his own community's topsy-turvy summer was wasted or not. After a pause he answers with one woman biting ginger and another sipping vinegar. The old eating-and-sleeping line supports a present test of the community, not a settled ranking of fieldwork below contemplative ease.

Anyone who can examine that may count as a monk with nothing extra to do; otherwise, do not waste the present time. Ordinary work is defended, while the claim that nothing further is required is itself tested. At the end of the retreat, Hansong Zhicao pairs clearing a field and sowing grain with a sea entered ever more deeply, then the midday meal and night's sleep with a mountain climbed ever higher. He imagines free movement and the capacity to act independently, even going beyond Buddha and patriarch. But if reputation and profit remain in mind and attachment to scenery persists, he changes register: clicking his teeth, he makes gestures of spraying water and drawing a talisman, ordering a rapid departure. The inherited line becomes his current contrast between deepening practice and a display still caught in attachments. The performance is not evidence that a literal spirit was expelled. Wanfeng raises the abbreviated summer exchange through Yangshan's reply that Weishan too has not wasted the season. His verse says father and son each present their family manner, yet their same dream in different beds is difficult to express. Without summer's end and autumn's beginning, how would meeting and speaking become so intimate? The meal-and-sleep answer is therefore read through the personal and seasonal encounter, not as a detached minimum schedule for every practitioner. This version does not retain the tongue gesture and further rebuke, so those details should not be described as part of its quoted turn. Duanqiao Miaolun first describes retreat confinement as an iron hammer and release as roads open in every direction. He then raises Weishan and Yangshan's exchange, including the tongue gesture and rebuke. Yangshan's unwasted summer means exposed feet and worn hands, he says; Weishan's means worn feet and exposed hands. Having balanced them through that reversal, he asks whether his own community's topsy-turvy summer was wasted or not. After a pause he answers with one woman biting ginger and another sipping vinegar. The old eating-and-sleeping line supports a present test of the community, not a settled ranking of fieldwork below contemplative ease.

Senses.Explanation: The sun rises in the east and at night sets in the west names an ordinary course that needs no hidden elaboration. Occurrences.Kwic: 進語，師便喝，僧禮拜，師乃云：天上無，地下無，我非我，吾非吾，雲門瞎棒，謾費分踈。大眾且道：釋迦老□□今在什麼處生？卓主丈云：洎乎錯下注脚。謝照了堂首座相訪，上堂。法界海慧，照了諸相□□。打鼓，侍者燒香。大眾凝立，山僧陞堂。戒香、定香、慧香、解脫香、解脫知見香。以手拈主丈放左邊，云：首座莫怪空踈。饒州東湖薦福禪寺海印和尚語錄饒州東湖薦福禪寺海印和尚語錄門人從心集入寺，上堂。僧問：鄱湖行盡到東湖，藹藹佳聲滿道途，莫莫堂前看號令，雲門普字趙州無。祝聖開堂，願聞法要。師云：總被禪客道了也。進云：與麼則一言用祝無疆壽，萬里無私賀太平。師云：又是從頭起。進云：此事且止，只如昔日僧問雲門：如何是正法眼？雲門答普，意旨如何？師云：天不言而四時行。僧云：又僧問趙州：狗子還有佛性也無？州云：無。又作麼生？師云：地不言而萬物生。僧云：與麼則一句合頭語，萬劫繫驢橛。師云：雲門普字趙州無。僧禮拜。又僧問云：諸佛出世，各坐一華，和尚開堂，有何祥瑞？師云：日出連山，月圓當戶。僧云：與麼則大眾沾恩去也。師云：更待何時？進云：只如昔日保壽開堂，三聖推出一僧，保壽便打，意旨如何？師云：風不來，樹不動。進云：三聖云：與麼為人，非但瞎却者僧眼，瞎却鎮州一城人眼去在。又作麼生？師云：金剛頂上鐵崑崙。進云：保壽擲下主丈便歸方丈，又且如何？師云：腦後見腮，莫與往來。進云：只如和尚今日開堂，學人問話，且道與三聖推僧是同是別？師云：莫將三歲竹，擬比萬年松。進云：與麼則一句逈超千聖外，松蘿不與月輪齊。師云：不經一事，不長一智。僧禮拜，師乃云：十八灘水月空寒，浩浩聲前誰辨主？三百里湖天晝靜，莫莫堂深親到時。舉一法則萬法全彰，示一機則群機普應，直得全彼全此、絕毫絕𨤲，逼塞虗空，非如非異。所言未既，驀忽伏虎祖師忍俊不禁出來道：長老，長老，絕江透湖，得得而來，將謂必新提唱、必異見聞，元來也只可可地。山僧只欵欵向他道：黃河三千年一度清。卓主丈一下。小參。目前無法，頭頂天，脚踏地；意在目前，眼見色，耳聞聲。不是目前法，甚麼處去也？非耳目之所到，元來只在這裡。伶俐漢，上上流，未舉先知，未言先領，直下轉得，便知一堤楊柳月，十里芰荷風。新薦福□□□境會，既不作境會，畢竟作什麼會？其或未辨□□，後五日看。舉：臺山路上有一婆子，每有僧問

Occurrences.Kwic: 天光直與水相通。解制，小參。翠巖一夏與兄弟東語西話，落盡眉毛，不覺精神十倍。臨濟遭黃檗打趂，中途疑著此事，再回終夏，換却多少鶻眼鷹睛。雲門道：和尚子莫妄想，天是天，地是地，山是山，水是水，僧是僧，俗是俗。良久，云：與我拈按山來，木人拍板雲中立，石女吹笙水上行。僧便問：學人見山是山、見水是水時如何？門云：三門為什麼騎佛殿從者裏過？西風一陣來，落葉兩三片。僧云：與麼則不妄想也。門云：還我話頭來，山頭石虎吼聲乾，海底驪龍拗角折。遂以主丈畫一畫，喝一喝。除夜，小參。無邊剎境，自它不隔於毫端；十世古今，始終不離於當念。山僧與諸人共汎一隻無底鐵舡，釋迦千百億化身坐舡頭、文殊堂裏萬菩薩坐舡尾，打鹽官鼓、唱德山歌，然後穿過東弗于逮也住千百億劫、北󳬂單越也住千百億劫、西瞿耶尼也住千百億劫、南贍部洲也住千百億劫，却回轉逕山寺裏法堂上，坐底依然自坐、立底依然自立。是汝諸人還信得及麼？良久，云：今夜今宵盡，明年明日迴，寒隨一夜去，春逐五更來。月講主火。日出連山，月圓當戶，大士講經竟，覿面無回互。擲火把云：火中鱉鼻蛇蛟，殺人無數。靈都寺火。無種靈苗火裏㘽，江南江北盡花開。栗蓬突出三千顆，曠劫無明當下灰。月上座火。通身是病，通身是藥。病去藥除，千峰月落。火裏鐵蛇橫，頭戴黃金角。曇芳和尚語錄卷上曇芳和尚語錄卷下曇芳和尚大龍翔集慶寺語錄曇芳和尚大龍翔集慶寺語錄常州路善權禪寺住持嗣法繼祖等編師於至正五年乙酉正月，在逕山寺，特奉聖旨，取二十九日入院。據室，拈主丈云：天下老和尚來也。以主丈畫一畫：釋迦老子、達磨大師，退後！退後！遂出陞座，拈香祝聖云：此一瓣香爇向寶爐，端為祝延大元聖主當今皇帝聖躬萬歲萬歲萬萬歲陛下，恭願道合兩儀，明逾二曜，本支百世，壽考萬年。遂斂衣敷坐，問答竟，乃云：吾本來茲土，傳法救迷情，一花開五葉，結果自然成。大眾還見麼？古釋迦不先，新彌勒不後，五風十雨共樂昇平，樵唱漁歌均陶至化，摩竭掩室，淨名杜詞，咲殺傍觀，德山入門便棒，臨濟入門便喝，總是祭鬼神茶飯，新龍翔到來合作麼生？卓主丈一下：是處是彌勒，無門無善財。行臺御史大夫也滅怯台率僚屬祈雨，請師陞座。師云：欲識佛性義，當觀時節因緣。時節若至，其理自彰。竪拂子云：看！看！娑竭羅龍王即今在龍翔拂子頭上現大自在身，油然作雲，沛然下雨，三世諸

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 扇曰：「黃庭經字真果好看。」僧曰：「我不看字。」師打一扇曰：「雲巖今日失利。」師與浴日遊抱子石，曰：「但有路可上，更高人也行。者裏為什麼到不得？」浴曰：「誰是不到者？」師曰：「幾不問過。」友嵩問：「善知識還入地獄也無？」師曰：「入。」嵩曰：「善知識如何也入地獄？」師曰：「知恩者少。」師一日與躍峰、載昇、別瀾、淡峰諸子，于法昌路次聞鷓鴣聲，問：「鷓鴣啼在深花裏，于三句內且道是那一句？」昇曰：「看腳下。」瀾曰：「且莫亂道。」峰曰：「莫教外人知。」峰曰：「總是道聽途說。」師曰：「總來喫棒。」師問友嵩曰：「我每日波波挈挈，為著阿誰？」嵩曰：「老不歇心。」師曰：「一總沒人情。」嵩曰：「若有人情，轉見禍事。」師曰：「怎消得！怎消得！」嵩作禮，師便打。僧問：「山花開似錦，梅雨落如絲。如何是龍華境？」師曰：「松濤十里吼如雷。」曰：「高踞獅王座，同歸不二門。如何是境中人？」師曰：「非聖非凡。」曰：「動容揚古路，不墮悄然機。如何是人中意？」師曰：「日出連山，月圓當戶。」東霽再參，師問：「從先驗過的不必拈出，試與我道箇新鮮句。」霽曰：「今日親見弁山。」師曰：「無你著眼處。」霽一喝，師曰：「你南詢一轉，幾多知識有鼻孔？幾多知識無鼻孔？」霽曰：「天上天下。」師曰：「你的鼻孔因甚不見？」霽曰：「瞞和尚不得。」師曰：「猶是昔時人。」霽又喝，師曰：「果然。」僧問：佛法遍在一切處，因甚大通智勝佛法不現前？師曰：「眼上不栽眉。曰：參禪學道貴乎妙悟，因甚趙州又道悟之一字直須吐卻？」師曰：「耳裏不著水。」曰：「獨羨追風駿不羈，迅然一吸空千里。」師曰：「晴空雖是無雲染，分付行人莫妄窺。」僧問：「如何是無生第一義？」師曰：「崑崙騎大象。」曰：「向上一竅，千聖不明。世尊陞座，因甚文殊獨覺？」師曰：「葉落知秋。」曰：「正是時節。」師便打。曰：「錦上更添花。」師曰：「屈棒也有人喫。」僧問：「大唐國裏行令，長安路上藏兵。即今天下太平，請師密示。」師曰：「新晴正喜鷓鴣啼。」僧問：「長慶因僧問：『如何是合聖之言？』慶曰：『山僧被者一問，直得口似匾擔。』今日有人問：如何指示？」師曰：「老僧口不在者裏。」僧曰：「恁麼則銕蛇橫古路。」師曰：「石虎吼當陽，你又作麼生？」僧無語，師便打。僧問：「如何是有佛處不得住？」師曰：「一度被

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 進語，師便喝，僧禮拜，師乃云：天上無，地下無，我非我，吾非吾，雲門瞎棒，謾費分踈。大眾且道：釋迦老□□今在什麼處生？卓主丈云：洎乎錯下注脚。謝照了堂首座相訪，上堂。法界海慧，照了諸相□□。打鼓，侍者燒香。大眾凝立，山僧陞堂。戒香、定香、慧香、解脫香、解脫知見香。以手拈主丈放左邊，云：首座莫怪空踈。饒州東湖薦福禪寺海印和尚語錄饒州東湖薦福禪寺海印和尚語錄門人從心集入寺，上堂。僧問：鄱湖行盡到東湖，藹藹佳聲滿道途，莫莫堂前看號令，雲門普字趙州無。祝聖開堂，願聞法要。師云：總被禪客道了也。進云：與麼則一言用祝無疆壽，萬里無私賀太平。師云：又是從頭起。進云：此事且止，只如昔日僧問雲門：如何是正法眼？雲門答普，意旨如何？師云：天不言而四時行。僧云：又僧問趙州：狗子還有佛性也無？州云：無。又作麼生？師云：地不言而萬物生。僧云：與麼則一句合頭語，萬劫繫驢橛。師云：雲門普字趙州無。僧禮拜。又僧問云：諸佛出世，各坐一華，和尚開堂，有何祥瑞？師云：日出連山，月圓當戶。僧云：與麼則大眾沾恩去也。師云：更待何時？進云：只如昔日保壽開堂，三聖推出一僧，保壽便打，意旨如何？師云：風不來，樹不動。進云：三聖云：與麼為人，非但瞎却者僧眼，瞎却鎮州一城人眼去在。又作麼生？師云：金剛頂上鐵崑崙。進云：保壽擲下主丈便歸方丈，又且如何？師云：腦後見腮，莫與往來。進云：只如和尚今日開堂，學人問話，且道與三聖推僧是同是別？師云：莫將三歲竹，擬比萬年松。進云：與麼則一句逈超千聖外，松蘿不與月輪齊。師云：不經一事，不長一智。僧禮拜，師乃云：十八灘水月空寒，浩浩聲前誰辨主？三百里湖天晝靜，莫莫堂深親到時。舉一法則萬法全彰，示一機則群機普應，直得全彼全此、絕毫絕𨤲，逼塞虗空，非如非異。所言未既，驀忽伏虎祖師忍俊不禁出來道：長老，長老，絕江透湖，得得而來，將謂必新提唱、必異見聞，元來也只可可地。山僧只欵欵向他道：黃河三千年一度清。卓主丈一下。小參。目前無法，頭頂天，脚踏地；意在目前，眼見色，耳聞聲。不是目前法，甚麼處去也？非耳目之所到，元來只在這裡。伶俐漢，上上流，未舉先知，未言先領，直下轉得，便知一堤楊柳月，十里芰荷風。新薦福□□□境會，既不作境會，畢竟作什麼會？其或未辨□□，後五日看。舉：臺山路上有一婆子，每有僧問

Senses.Explanation: Striking the third night watch at midday overturns ordinary time in an impossible Chan image. Senses.Explanation: "Strike the third watch at noon; face south and see the Northern Dipper" joins two impossible coordinates. The four masters use the paired dislocation as a teaching reply or image. Fushi speaks it after comparing the three teachings; Yinyuan sets it in a compact hall verse. Baiyu gives it as an answer to who shares the clarity he has described; Chisong uses it in an address marking his teacher record.

Senses.Explanation: The suns unbroken daily rising and setting answers from the ordinary visible cycle rather than a hidden cosmology. Hanxiu, Huqiu, Yuechuang, and Yikui each turn the line to a different current occasion: solstice, human mortality, memorial address, and year-end time. The retained fifth witness is a separate present sermon. Retained public meaning is supported by independent present uses in recorded discourse.

Senses.Explanation: Every day is a good day (日日是好日) is a short answer inside exchanges about non-choice. In Chushi Fanqi’s record, an unnamed monk offers “every year is a good year, every day is a good day” (年年是好年，日日是好日) and Chushi replies; Jifei Ruyi gives “every day is a good day” (日日是好日) as his answer to a question about not choosing. A parallel in a transmission record corroborates the formula without determining its sense.

Senses.Note: Linye, Foyuan, Yuelin, and Haiyin each voice the complete pair in their own present turns. Haiyin recalls Yunmen shorter good-day answer before making a new verse with both clauses. The public head has the day clause alone; the added time clause presses the question into each occasion. The sources do not promise that every event feels pleasant.

Occurrences.Kwic: ，無位真人汗如雨。』」師云：「古人雖是千差掃蕩，未能驚殺多人。且道今日事作麼生？」卓拄杖：「今朝五月望，黃鶯啼柳上，明月與清風，諦當甚諦當？打動震天鼉，德山歌要唱。報諸人，休放況，苦雨酸風陣陣來，打溼陳年底寶藏。大眾，既是各懷寶藏，因甚被他打溼？不挂浮囊巨海登，無位真人是什麼像狀？」喝一喝，下座。示眾。「鵲來頭上語諵諵，雲向眼前疊翠三。關捩盡情如瞥落，不須靈利更加參。」上堂。「雷門之下，布鼓難鳴。度刃奔流，過風疾焰。搆得搆不得，豎四橫三。是境不是境，蘆花雪月。只如無價大寶光中，脣鋒不涉，散遍十方世界。應用無虧，吞吐五蘊山河。大眾，若據法者，當如法說。且道遞相告報是汝諸人，還會麼？」良久曰：「寧可清貧自樂，不作濁富多憂。」拍膝一下。上堂。「威鳳山前雲出入，駟馬橋頭浪捲舒。更有龍門高萬仞，是誰點額泊清虛。正當恁麼時，由茲發育，自此流通。理隨事變，事逐理融。只如德山耀大法眼，臨濟轟大法雷，諸人不得蹉過。」以拄杖卓一卓，喝一喝。上堂。「日日是好日，時時是好時，破鏡不重照，落花難上枝。推遷四象，日月旋流，檢點將來，自救不了。豈不見白蓮池畔香映宛然，駟馬橋頭長安逼直？悟則事同一家，迷乃萬別千差。即今還有迷悟者麼？」以拂子擊禪床：「著甚來由？」趙觀察設齋，請上堂。「時維中元節，地官曾解結。空闊互相交，夜蟬鳴不歇。祖師西來意，諸人瞥不瞥？清淨總持門，是甚繫驢橛？棘曲嫌松直，烏玄笑鵠白。皎皎長空天地殊，熙熙萬姓歌唐業。」擊禪床，下座。上堂。舉：「系南禪師示眾云：『禪不禪，道不道，三寸舌頭胡亂掃，昨夜日輪飄桂花，今朝月窟生芝草。阿呵呵！萬兩黃金無處討，一向絕思量，諸法不相到。』」師云：「古人恁麼提持，有甚麼實處？若據超佛越祖之機，莫作秋深長夜之境。昭覺不是乘時就便，豈假節目強生？」乃拈拄杖：「禪不禪，道不道，豎亞面門非作造，昨夜泥牛飲海乾，今朝木馬追風跑。阿呵呵！祖師窟是野狐窖，驀地喚將來，打個解𨁝跳。諸大眾！不是埋沒諸人，者裏何嘗易討？」復卓拄杖：「毘婆尸佛早留心，直至而今不得妙。」誕日，上堂。「桂蕊篩篩金落地，月華冉冉玉鋪奇，若謂吾曹生面目，今朝覿面為提撕。諸大眾，莫疑猜，糞掃堆頭珠拾來，人人有分如薦得，無限勞生眼豁開。」復舉：「金峰禪師云：『山僧二十年前有老婆心，二十年後無老婆心。』

Occurrences.Kwic: 噓一聲。師乃云：諸法空為座，處此為說法，法法不隱藏，清風生六合。一著高一著，一步闊一步，黃面老瞿曇、西來箇達磨，盡向者裏納一場敗闕。敢問大眾：那裏是他納敗闕處？毗婆尸佛早留心，直至而今不得妙。復舉：世尊一日陞座，大眾集定，文殊白槌云：世尊說法竟。世尊便下座。大眾還知古聖落處麼？動絃別曲，葉落知秋，風生大野，水向東流。當晚小參，云：聖因古蘭若，湖邊絕瀟洒，知他幾百年，已屬斯人也。以至東弗于逮、西瞿耶尼、南瞻部洲、北󳬂單越，置于掌握之中，擲大千於方外，又作麼生？拍膝，云：風光都買盡，不費一文錢。復舉：誌公令人傳語思大：和尚何不下山教化眾生？一向目視雲漢作什麼？思大云：三世諸佛被我一口吞盡，何處更有眾生可度？師云：要識思大麼？貧恨一身多。上堂：日可冷，月可熱，眾魔不能壞真說。且道如何是真說？十語九中不如一默。上堂：古鏡闊一丈，虗空闊一丈。竪起拂子云：這箇在虗空內，虗空外。參！上堂：結夏又十日，箇事作麼生？無風荷葉動，決定有魚行。上堂：日日是好日，時時是好時，為什麼人人向脚跟下蹉過？只為分明極，翻令所得遲。廣度和尚至，上堂：真正舉揚，法堂前草深一丈，有如是作略、有如是牓樣，箇是阿誰？廣度和尚以拂子擊禪床，下座。上堂，舉：僧問趙州：狗子還有佛性也無？州云：無。師云：斷人性命，不勞餘刃。四海一家，風恬浪靜。慈懿皇后大祥，陞座。此世不移動，彼世不改變，惟一堅密身，一切塵中現。上堂：今朝十月一，開爐是此日。趙州賓主話，聖因為拈出。拈也拈了也，說也說了也。畢竟如何？歸堂向火去。承天禮和尚遺書至，上堂：去去實不去，來來實不來。去來如夢幻，虗空絕點埃。正恁麼時，同庵和尚在甚處？竪起拂子，云：佛祖位中留不住，夜來依舊宿蘆花。上堂。五日上堂，朝朝入室，三八念誦，叢林規式。喝一喝，云：美食不中飽人喫。上堂：本無迷悟人，只要今日了。了了了了了，面南看北斗。咄！上堂：熱即取凉，寒即向火，飢即喫飯，困即打睡。莫將無事會，無事困人心。住平江府承天能仁禪寺語錄住平江府承天能仁禪寺語錄侍者法璹編上堂：世尊三昧，迦葉不知。迦葉三昧，阿難不知。阿難三昧，商那和修不知。從上諸聖三昧，互相不知。敢問諸人，且道不知箇什麼？若是俊流，便知落處。其或未然，莫將閑學解，埋沒祖師心。上堂，舉賓頭盧尊者因阿育王問：承聞尊者親見佛

Occurrences.Kwic: 其物，忘其情，空而妙，虗而靈。正恁麼，何似生？回機轉位，異類中行。幾度黑風翻大浪，未曾聞道釣舟傾。上堂：至德如流，上善若水。一塵入正受，諸塵三昧起。洗面摸著鼻，喫茶濕却觜。忽有箇出來問：久嚮薦福，元來只說古人舊話。只向他道：熟處難忘。上堂：八尺釘丈二楔，著在眼中，撼搖不得。薦福門下，妙在轉處，誰是知音？不見三祖大師道：纔有是非，紛然失心。乃擲下主丈。頌古頌古僧問雲門：樹凋葉落時如何？門云：體露金風。秋風葉落動凉颸，堪笑雲門跛阿師。銷盡浮華到真實，不知開口落今時。僧問香林：如何是衲衣下事？林云：臘月火燒山。香林臘月火燒山，黑齒波師帶白環。唐梵一時俱譯了，肯將名字落人間。僧問趙州云：未有世間，早有此性；世界懷時，此性不壞。如何是不壞底性？州云：四大五蘊。僧云：此猶是壞底，如何是不壞底？州云：四大五蘊。老諗年尊閱事多，清平世界樂無何。一身儱侗無邊表，地覆天翻也只那。雲門示眾云：十五日以前不問汝，十五日以後道將一句來。代云：日日是好日。日日是好日，時時是好時。鯨吞海水盡，露出珊瑚枝。僧問古德：冬至後日長多少？德云：長一絲。佛法長多少？德云：一線長。佛法一線長，青天謾度量。絲頭纔咬斷，紅日上扶桑。泐潭常禪師一日面壁而坐，南泉來見，撫師背一下，潭云：誰？泉云：某甲。潭云：如何？泉云：也尋常。潭云：汝何多事？言中有響語藏鋒，一色明邊分異同。月棹各撑俱到岸，不知身在草窠中。谷隱性空和尚因僧問：靈山一會，何異今日？性空云：不異今日。僧云：不異底事作麼生？性空云：如來密語，迦葉不傳。酬應相於理不乖，泯然一種似平懷。及乎話到聱訛處，樹上心肝不帶來。偈頌偈頌水心水心一源見徹萬波翻，澄不清兮撓不渾。識浪境風俱列下，鑄成滄海鐵崑崙。靈竺靈竺鷲嶺人天鴨聽雷，大僊密付絕纖埃，飛來小朵從何有？兩㵎琮琤一逕開。雲頂雲頂溶溶洩洩復閒閒，來者從教斫額看，起滅無蹤空絕迹，竪摩醯眼照人間。震上人震上人惡辣兒孫喪本宗，向空拏撮便填空，震威一喝無今古，百丈馬師皆患聾。刀鑷沈生刀鑷沈生空彈霜鑷到巖扄，覿面難將妙手呈，雨洗秋容同澹泊，遠山無限佛頭青。遠上人遠上人遠來一見便相違，竹外清風聽者稀。却是晚鴻知此意，數聲清唳入雲微。秀上人之仰秀上人之仰碧巖千尺瀑雪落，峭壁萬疊峰雲寒，一笻雙履超聲外，圓相暗機誰共看？無相無相意地消

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 噓一聲。師乃云：諸法空為座，處此為說法，法法不隱藏，清風生六合。一著高一著，一步闊一步，黃面老瞿曇、西來箇達磨，盡向者裏納一場敗闕。敢問大眾：那裏是他納敗闕處？毗婆尸佛早留心，直至而今不得妙。復舉：世尊一日陞座，大眾集定，文殊白槌云：世尊說法竟。世尊便下座。大眾還知古聖落處麼？動絃別曲，葉落知秋，風生大野，水向東流。當晚小參，云：聖因古蘭若，湖邊絕瀟洒，知他幾百年，已屬斯人也。以至東弗于逮、西瞿耶尼、南瞻部洲、北󳬂單越，置于掌握之中，擲大千於方外，又作麼生？拍膝，云：風光都買盡，不費一文錢。復舉：誌公令人傳語思大：和尚何不下山教化眾生？一向目視雲漢作什麼？思大云：三世諸佛被我一口吞盡，何處更有眾生可度？師云：要識思大麼？貧恨一身多。上堂：日可冷，月可熱，眾魔不能壞真說。且道如何是真說？十語九中不如一默。上堂：古鏡闊一丈，虗空闊一丈。竪起拂子云：這箇在虗空內，虗空外。參！上堂：結夏又十日，箇事作麼生？無風荷葉動，決定有魚行。上堂：日日是好日，時時是好時，為什麼人人向脚跟下蹉過？只為分明極，翻令所得遲。廣度和尚至，上堂：真正舉揚，法堂前草深一丈，有如是作略、有如是牓樣，箇是阿誰？廣度和尚以拂子擊禪床，下座。上堂，舉：僧問趙州：狗子還有佛性也無？州云：無。師云：斷人性命，不勞餘刃。四海一家，風恬浪靜。慈懿皇后大祥，陞座。此世不移動，彼世不改變，惟一堅密身，一切塵中現。上堂：今朝十月一，開爐是此日。趙州賓主話，聖因為拈出。拈也拈了也，說也說了也。畢竟如何？歸堂向火去。承天禮和尚遺書至，上堂：去去實不去，來來實不來。去來如夢幻，虗空絕點埃。正恁麼時，同庵和尚在甚處？竪起拂子，云：佛祖位中留不住，夜來依舊宿蘆花。上堂。五日上堂，朝朝入室，三八念誦，叢林規式。喝一喝，云：美食不中飽人喫。上堂：本無迷悟人，只要今日了。了了了了了，面南看北斗。咄！上堂：熱即取凉，寒即向火，飢即喫飯，困即打睡。莫將無事會，無事困人心。住平江府承天能仁禪寺語錄住平江府承天能仁禪寺語錄侍者法璹編上堂：世尊三昧，迦葉不知。迦葉三昧，阿難不知。阿難三昧，商那和修不知。從上諸聖三昧，互相不知。敢問諸人，且道不知箇什麼？若是俊流，便知落處。其或未然，莫將閑學解，埋沒祖師心。上堂，舉賓頭盧尊者因阿育王問：承聞尊者親見佛

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 其物，忘其情，空而妙，虗而靈。正恁麼，何似生？回機轉位，異類中行。幾度黑風翻大浪，未曾聞道釣舟傾。上堂：至德如流，上善若水。一塵入正受，諸塵三昧起。洗面摸著鼻，喫茶濕却觜。忽有箇出來問：久嚮薦福，元來只說古人舊話。只向他道：熟處難忘。上堂：八尺釘丈二楔，著在眼中，撼搖不得。薦福門下，妙在轉處，誰是知音？不見三祖大師道：纔有是非，紛然失心。乃擲下主丈。頌古頌古僧問雲門：樹凋葉落時如何？門云：體露金風。秋風葉落動凉颸，堪笑雲門跛阿師。銷盡浮華到真實，不知開口落今時。僧問香林：如何是衲衣下事？林云：臘月火燒山。香林臘月火燒山，黑齒波師帶白環。唐梵一時俱譯了，肯將名字落人間。僧問趙州云：未有世間，早有此性；世界懷時，此性不壞。如何是不壞底性？州云：四大五蘊。僧云：此猶是壞底，如何是不壞底？州云：四大五蘊。老諗年尊閱事多，清平世界樂無何。一身儱侗無邊表，地覆天翻也只那。雲門示眾云：十五日以前不問汝，十五日以後道將一句來。代云：日日是好日。日日是好日，時時是好時。鯨吞海水盡，露出珊瑚枝。僧問古德：冬至後日長多少？德云：長一絲。佛法長多少？德云：一線長。佛法一線長，青天謾度量。絲頭纔咬斷，紅日上扶桑。泐潭常禪師一日面壁而坐，南泉來見，撫師背一下，潭云：誰？泉云：某甲。潭云：如何？泉云：也尋常。潭云：汝何多事？言中有響語藏鋒，一色明邊分異同。月棹各撑俱到岸，不知身在草窠中。谷隱性空和尚因僧問：靈山一會，何異今日？性空云：不異今日。僧云：不異底事作麼生？性空云：如來密語，迦葉不傳。酬應相於理不乖，泯然一種似平懷。及乎話到聱訛處，樹上心肝不帶來。偈頌偈頌水心水心一源見徹萬波翻，澄不清兮撓不渾。識浪境風俱列下，鑄成滄海鐵崑崙。靈竺靈竺鷲嶺人天鴨聽雷，大僊密付絕纖埃，飛來小朵從何有？兩㵎琮琤一逕開。雲頂雲頂溶溶洩洩復閒閒，來者從教斫額看，起滅無蹤空絕迹，竪摩醯眼照人間。震上人震上人惡辣兒孫喪本宗，向空拏撮便填空，震威一喝無今古，百丈馬師皆患聾。刀鑷沈生刀鑷沈生空彈霜鑷到巖扄，覿面難將妙手呈，雨洗秋容同澹泊，遠山無限佛頭青。遠上人遠上人遠來一見便相違，竹外清風聽者稀。却是晚鴻知此意，數聲清唳入雲微。秀上人之仰秀上人之仰碧巖千尺瀑雪落，峭壁萬疊峰雲寒，一笻雙履超聲外，圓相暗機誰共看？無相無相意地消

Senses.Explanation: Goodness is stated of both the day and the time within it. Linye and Foyuan use the linked formula in present hall talks, leaving no easy refuge in the passage of time. Senses.PreferredTarget: Sun and moon brighten the virtue of heaven; mountains and rivers grace the imperial dwelling.
AlternateTargets: Sun and moon illumine heavenly virtue; mountains and rivers lend grandeur to the imperial court.

sun moon heaven virtue mountains rivers ruler Zen
Senses.Note: Hongzhi uses the exact pair as his answer to a question about the ruler; Baichi and Huiyue answer New Year blessing requests with it; Buyan and Pufu voice it in their own ceremonial turns. The courtly language is part of those settings and does not by itself name a monastery or a specific emperor. An unnamed monk repeats the pair in J28nB203, but that question is not counted as a named master use.

Occurrences.Kwic: 進云：「有甚麼限量？」師云：「東西十萬，南北八千。」乃云：「明不得，狀不得，瓦解冰消；事一然，理一然，天高地厚。只要人人直下承當，箇箇就中委悉。如委悉得，兩箇鴛鴦池中獨立；其或不然，一雙孤鴈撲地高飛。」復舉：「五祖演上堂云：『多說不如少說，少說不如不說。』演祖大似鸚鵡能言，道得不知有多少，俱說了又道不說。華岩今日多也不說，少也不說，只如不說之說又作麼生？」良久，云：「今古罕聞。」庚水母難，請上堂。「松柏南山足可論，一番春至一番新，更有虛空無比相，風歌雨唱曲長生。只如那吒析骨還父、析肉還母，然後為父母說法又作麼生？」良久，云：「粉骨碎身未足酬，一句了然超百億。」元日，上堂。問：「如何是新年頭佛法？」師云：「萬頃白雲鋪錦繡，一輪紅日挂金毬。」進云：「恁麼一人有慶，兆民賴之。」師云：「薰大香一瓣，誰人不點頭？」乃云：「新年頭佛法有，海宇雲霞散彩，江程梅柳生輝；新年頭佛法無，道泰不傳天子令，時清休唱太平歌。只如不落新舊有無一句作麼生道？日月光天德，山河壯帝居。」解制，上堂。「百日期中，無繩自縛；三條椽下，有口難言。挨到今日，飲氣吞聲，欲去不去、欲住不住，不免放開便道，任意縱橫。或於十字街頭、三家村裡，和其光、同其塵，恁麼也得；或於孤峰頂上、林下水邊，閉其門、塞其兌，恁麼不恁麼也得。還委悉麼？莫道華岩山勢險，前途猶有最高峰。」上堂。問：「如何是父母未生前？」師云：「石筍抽條。」進云：「如何是已生後？」師云：「只是不識羞。」云：「已生未生時如何？」師云：「秋夜月明天在水，波光卻與月輪齊。」乃云：「德山托缽上法堂。雲在嶺頭閒不徹，水流澗下太茫生。雪峰道：『鐘未鳴，鼓未響，托缽向甚處去？』養子不及父，家門一世衰。德山便歸方丈。憐兒不覺醜，徒負缽盂忙。岩頭云：『老漢未會末後句在。』戴月瑤枝秀，扶危碧樹高。山云：『你不肯老僧那？』頭密啟其意。一片白雲橫谷口，許多歸鳥盡迷巢。次日，上堂。果與往日不同。心不負人，面無慚色。岩頭撫掌笑云：『且喜老漢會得末後句也，他後天下人不柰伊何。雖然如是，也只得三年活。』謾道爺貧連子苦，須知家富小兒嬌。」遂顧左右，云：「看他德山父子與麼玉轉珠回，擲地金聲，未免自揚家醜。只如會得底末後句也只得三年活，又是什麼道理？」良久，云：「玉宇秋高無界限，無逾萬映一輪孤。」

Senses.Explanation: A fixed list-name for the shining host of the sky, traveling with the rivers and grounds below. Yunmen Wenyan asks what they call the rivers and grounds, the luminaries, and the four elements, then calls his own words a village wife's talk fit to be dragged off the steps, Foyan Qingyuan reads the linked pearls of the luminaries at the imperial anniversary as the fruit of the sovereign's virtue and comes down from the seat to dance his ten thousand years, Chijue Daochong hangs the luminaries with the rivers, the myriad forms, and color and emptiness on the three turns of his senior fellow, Hengchuan Rugong calls the rivers and grounds waves of the boundless nature sea, the luminaries waves, and the noses of all buddhas soaked soft in it, and Chushi Fanqi sings the ground tilted northwest with the luminaries tied to a sky that never lowers, while every nose stays straight and every eye level. Wuyi Yuanlai takes the sky as mouth, the sea as tongue, the luminaries as adornment, and the rivers as audience, and still no one hears, Yi'an Shanzan rules the rivers and the luminaries what the wondrous bright true nature shows, with no fault to find, Muchen Daomin lets all be Maitreya and sends the rivers and the luminaries back to being themselves, Yuan'an Liao plows under even the earth, the sky, the luminaries, and the grass and trees till nothing above can shelter and nothing below can block, and Guantao Daqi casts the whole ten directions as one furnace into which the luminaries and all that flies and burrows enter and melt into one body.

Senses.PreferredTarget: Sun and moon pass across the sky yet make no circuit
SearchAliases: sun and moon pass across the sky yet make no circuit
Senses.Note: The phrase belongs to an older four-part saying in which wind, rivers, wild horses, and the heavenly bodies move without a separate fixed motion. Feiyin invokes it while discussing old and new time. Shenfeng challenges his listeners to recognize it at a staff gesture. Baiyu raises a whisk against the assumption that seasons and birth alter what he shows. Yuanan uses it as one of four lines on arising and ceasing, and Hansong asks where life and death can be located after saying it. Their turns use visible change to make the paradox answerable.

SearchAliases: daily tasks no different naturally in accord
Senses.Note: Pang Yun gives this pair at the start of a verse answering Shitou’s question about what he does each day. The verse closes with carrying water and gathering firewood, so the ordinary setting matters. Miyun applies the line to a layperson’s buying and selling; Tianyin asks how Pang could utter a verse after saying daily affairs left no room for speech. Lianyue presses another layperson to explain what “no different” means, while Linye warns that merely choosing this phrase as an answer misses the matter. The words describe accord in daily activity, not a private claim that Pang alone is special.

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: No.1336龐居士語錄卷上節度使于頔編集優婆塞世燈重梓語錄襄州居士龐蘊，字道玄，衡州衡陽縣人也。世本儒業，少悟塵勞，志求真諦。唐貞元初，謁石頭禪師，乃問：不與萬法為侶者是甚麼人？頭以手掩其口，豁然有省。一日，石頭問曰：子見老僧以來，日用事作麼生？士曰：若問日用事，即無開口處。頭曰：知子恁麼，方始問子。士乃呈偈曰：日用事無別，唯吾自偶諧。頭頭非取捨，處處沒張乖。朱紫誰為號？丘山絕點埃。神通并妙用，運水與搬柴。頭然之，曰：子以緇耶？素耶？士曰：願從所慕。遂不剃染。居士後之江西，參馬祖大師，問曰：不與萬法為侶者是什麼人？祖曰：待汝一口吸盡西江水，即向汝道。士於言下頓領玄旨，遂呈偈，有心空及第之句，乃留駐參承二載。有偈曰：有男不婚，有女不嫁，大家團圞頭，共說無生話。士一日又問祖曰：不昧本來人，請師高著眼。祖直下󳬇，士曰：一等沒絃琹，惟師彈得妙。祖直上󳬇，士禮拜，祖歸方丈，士隨後曰：適來弄巧成拙。士一日又問祖曰：如水無筋骨，能勝萬斛舟，此理如何？祖曰：這裏無水亦無舟，說什麼筋骨？居士到藥山禪師，山問曰：一乘中還著得這箇事麼？士曰：某甲祇管日求升合，不知還著得麼？山曰：道居士不見石頭得麼？士曰：拈一放一，未為好手。山曰：老僧住持事繁。士珍重便出。山曰：拈一放一，的是好手。士曰：好箇一乘問宗，今日失却也。山曰：是！是！居士因辭藥山，山命十禪客相送至門首，士乃指空中雪曰：好雪片片，不落別處。有全禪客曰：落在甚處？士遂與一掌，全曰：也不得草草。士曰：恁麼稱禪客，閻羅老子未放你在。全曰：居士作麼生？士又掌曰：眼見如盲，口說如瘂。居士到齊峰，纔入院，峰曰：箇俗人頻頻入院，討箇

Senses.Explanation: Pang’s answer finds accord in the acts of an ordinary day. Pang answers Shitou with a verse; Miyun applies its opening to a layperson’s buying and selling. Tianyin questions the verse’s very utterance, Linye rejects slogan use, and Lianyue asks another layperson to explain it.

Senses.PreferredTarget: Daily affairs are nothing apart; I find accord in them myself
SearchAliases: daily affairs are nothing apart; i find accord in them myself
Senses.Note: Pang Yun says daily affairs are no different and that he himself meets them in accord. Shiqi brings the verse into a spring sermon, pointing to blossoms and water. Feiyin warns against resting in Pang’s words; Baichi asks his listeners to account for the saying in their own day. Tianran presses hardest against claiming that ordinary activity is enough merely because one can recite the line.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J28/J28nB215.xml). Collected Echoes on Verse Commentaries to Old Cases (頌古合響集): Zhaozhou Congshen utters the exact headword-bearing wording in the complete source unit.

Senses.Explanation: The clay buddha is a materially clay image in Zhaozhou’s water/furnace/fire set, and Yuanwu explicitly predicates that it dissolves in water. Literally, a buddha image made of clay or mud. The term is attested. Its dominant use is Zhaozhou's four-line saying: 'a gold buddha does not pass through a furnace; a wooden buddha does not pass through fire; a clay buddha does not pass through water; the true buddha sits inside' (金佛不度爐，木佛不度火，泥佛不度水，真佛內裏坐). Yuanwu supplies the direct material predicate: 'if a clay buddha crosses water, it dissolves' (泥佛若渡水。則爛却了也。), alongside gold melting in a furnace and wood burning in fire. Later records preserve the four lines, verse on each line, invert them, and ask them as separate interview questions. Answers to 'What is a clay buddha not crossing water?' (如何是泥佛不度水) include 'submerge it over its head and kill it' (沒頭浸殺), 'it cannot be soaked', 'soak it but it does not dissolve' (浸他不爛), and 'ten times ten thousand in every direction'. A layman also asks, 'What is a clay buddha turning around?' (如何是泥佛轉身); the recorded answer is 'lose money in the water and dredge for it in the river' (水裏失錢河裏撈). These answers are retained as the corpus's use range without assigning a single unstated gloss to them.

Senses.Explanation: More mud makes a larger clay buddha, just as higher water raises a boat. Wuzu Fayan lets that obvious proportion stand by itself; Ying'an Tanhua repeats it and immediately asks whether clear explanation has reached personal arrival. Wuzu Fayan gives the pair by itself in a hall address after saying that spiritual powers lack nothing and an accomplished person needs no chatter. The line lets increasing material and increasing result answer without further explanation. Ying'an Tanhua immediately warns that even a perfectly clear account still requires personally arriving once; when he asks what follows that arrival, he answers that reason does not depend on a loud voice. In Tianzeneng's record an unnamed questioner quotes the pair before asking why the ground of actuality admits not one mote, and three monks answer separately. Yuejian uses the saying during entry into the hermitage while addressing Weituo: mud, water, buddha, and boat retain their ordinary proportional relation, but the public question is what such ready-made correctness accomplishes in the present encounter.

Senses.Explanation: The clay ox entering the sea is an impossible-animal image of disappearance beyond observation or recovery. Yongjue completes it with 'no one sees it,' and Lingyan with 'leaving no trace.' Baiyun's verse shifts attention to what follows: after the clay ox enters the sea, gathering and dispersal are as insubstantial as wind over bubbles. The phrase can answer a doctrinal position or appear in verse, but those are uses of one stock image rather than separate senses. The wording itself does not require one narrow doctrinal equation; its stable floor is complete, traceless disappearance. Hanyue reshapes the mud-ox image in his own verse of reply to a lay student.

Senses.Explanation: A mud ox bellowing at the moon gives voice and upward address to an earthen animal that cannot move or cry. Chan masters pair it with a wooden horse neighing in the wind, use it in questions about Chan and the Way, and place it in verses where ordinary causal expectations are suspended. Yinyuan Longqi pairs “the mud ox bellows at the moon” with “the wooden horse neighs in the wind.” Meixi Du’s interlocutor asks whether the mud ox and wooden horse constitute the Way; Meixi answers with the paired sand-and-water saying. Gaofeng Yuanmiao’s verse makes the mud ox face the wind and bellow at the moon while warning against a mistaken fixed measure. Yuancheng’s hall address brings a one-legged mud ox bellowing at the moon beside a three-headed wooden horse. Yichu Yuan says the mud ox opens the gold-lock barrier while the wooden horse breaks the silver mountain iron wall.

Senses.Note: The formula travels in two shapes, the plain (泥裏有刺) and the prefixed (爛泥裏有刺, rotten mud), thirteen of the eighteen retained rows carrying the prefix. Its partners are the needle in the silk floss (綿裏有針, paired by Tianqi Benrui) and the rice-side partners (米裏有虫， 米中有鐵， 米裏添沙)， none of which has an entry of its own in the public termbase; the locative variant (泥中有刺, 38 exact hits) is a different graph sequence and is not counted under this headword. Retained rows span twelve works from the old verse through the Kangxi years, and no lamp record is kept: every retained use is carried in a Tier-2 record.

Senses.Explanation: The formula (泥裏有刺, there is a thorn in the mud) states the ground. Its oldest named carrier is Pang Yun's verse, quoted whole by Chushi Fanqi — if you want to know the meaning inside this, there is a thorn in the mud, an iron boat floats on the water, a bearded man has no mustache. Baoning Renyong answers with it at question time: asked what the Way is, there is a thorn in the mud; asked what the person in the Way is, be careful not to step on it. Yuanwu Keqin makes it the whole answer to a question about Zhizang's deflection and again the ruling word on Subhuti's I-cannot-say; Dahui Zonggao answers the Jingqing two-drips-sound exchange with it; and in the Blue Cliff Record Yuanwu judges even Xuedou's grandmother's kindness with it — but alas, a thorn in the mud. The answer class. Baoning Renyong's exchange runs three questions: what is the Buddha — the fire-nearest scorches first; what is the Way — there is a thorn in the mud; what is the person in the Way — be careful not to step on it. Yuanwu Keqin, pressed at the seat on the Mazu-Zhizang-Baizhang exchange, answers Zhizang's go-ask-Hai deflection with the formula alone, and keeps going: Baizhang's I-get-lost-here draws a turtle boring through a wall, Mazu's white-head-black-head a frontier general's order. Dahui Zonggao answers the Jingqing two-drips-sound (兩滴聲) question the same way: the two-drips-sound questioner quotes Jingqing's beings-inverted-chasing-objects, and Dahui answers, rotten mud with a thorn in it. And Yushan Shangsi, taken down the vine-and-tree chain to Guishan's loud laugh returning to his quarters, answers, guard against the rotten mud with a thorn in it. The verdict class. Yuanwu's turning-words on the Shariputra-Subhuti dream dialogue rule line by line — hush, hush; this meaning is deep, I cannot say it, rotten mud with a thorn in it; passing it to another gets you nowhere. Baiyan Fu turns the formula on Kasyapa's white-mallet: elders say the venerable one failed to hold the line — not so, he had no answer, and the thorn sits in the mud with great stakes involved. Nouyun Zhenshi rules on Kasyapa walking in the mud, asked by a novice why he works himself: the venerable one has a thorn in his mud, the novice's eyes get dust — then gives his own answer to the same question and asks the assembly whether there is a difference. Yinyuan Longqi works Lingyun's peach-blossom verse line by line — thirty years seeking a sword, labor without merit; since seeing the blossoms, specks in the eye — and on Xuansha's well-said-indeed he sets the thorn in the mud, then asks whether Xuansha himself is through. Sanyi Mingyu rules on the Puzhao exchange: had Puzhao met the question with a crown-of-head staff the lineage would not be so lonely — instead he said it limp and soft, and yet there is a thorn in the rotten mud; makers know it. The commentary class. In the Blue Cliff Record Yuanwu Keqin judges the old master of the case of the two venerables who answered alike: asked long after whether he had sanctioned them, the case's old master said yes, sanctioned — but no patriarch-coming-west meaning in it; the commentator rules with the formula — a thorn in the mud, letting it pass gives it away, already fallen to second — and adds that had it been him: not yet sanctioned. On Xuedou's verse about not recognizing one's own pure dharmakaya he rules again — Xuedou faulted him for a grandmother's kindness, but alas, a thorn in the mud — and then sets Dongshan's three roads before the beginners. The warning class. Dahui's sermon on Linji's sayings, self-named Miaoxi in the cut: the ancients hung out a device — was that idle talk? Know there is a thorn in the rotten mud; and he goes on to Kefu the ascetic, who did understand Linji and asked the four alternatives. Chushi Fanqi instructs the assembly: within the teaching-vehicle too it is greatly fearful — a thorn in the mud; step on it and you will know — and then sets the Huayan image of the great sutra-scroll inside a dust-grain beside it. Juelang Daosheng closes his address on head-to-head deceiving — starving in the rice-basket, dying of thirst in the great sea — with the question: do you now know that in the heaven of neither-perception-nor-non-perception there is a thorn in the rotten mud? Ah! Watch your feet. The graders and the couplet. Shiyu Mingfang judges Qianfeng's two-part saying at the winter solstice in three moves: raise one, the feet cross the water unwet; do not raise two, rotten mud with a thorn in it; let pass one move, the sparrowhawk cannot catch it — and where is the fallen-to-second now?. Nouyun Zhenshi quotes his grandfather-teacher Poshan Haiming's three first-sentences — first sentence realized, carving a sore in good flesh; second, digging a hole in empty space; third, a thorn in the mud — then answers with three of his own and asks the assembly, same or different?. Tianqi Benrui's couplet verdict on the old woman who drowned her seventh son after Yantou struck her: needle in the silk floss, thorn in the mud — this old woman is strange indeed; without Yantou it would have been hard to withstand. The warning's extension. Juyun Chuiwan Guangzhen tells his assembly not to take his long words for an old monk's passed-down password: know there is a thorn in the rotten mud, and do not keep cradling the child that does not cry, dragging on like that — there is something in the back garden.

Senses.Note: The saying calls the single word "knowing" a gate to the many wonders. In these Chan uses it is deliberately paired with the contrary line that knowing is a gate to many troubles. The masters ask what kind of knowing is at issue, and whether one can avoid clinging to either formula.

Senses.Explanation: "The single word knowing is the gate to myriad wonders" is a positive Chan formula about awareness. Masters often set it against the opposite claim that knowing opens the gate to troubles, making the kind of knowing the real question. Poshan states both gate formulas in advice to a practitioner. Shiyu distinguishes ordinary knowing from the knowing of one who has realized. Yinyuan asks hearers to pass both formulations. Tianran challenges his audience to reconcile them rather than choosing one as a slogan.

Senses.PreferredTarget: The single word “knowing” is the gate to many troubles
AlternateTargets: That one word, “know,” opens the door to countless troubles
Senses.Note: The warning targets the certainty a person takes from saying “I know.” Several masters put it beside the opposed line that calls knowing a gate to wonders. Their juxtaposition makes the audience test what sort of knowing is at issue instead of choosing one slogan as a rule.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB177.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Poshan. Poshan Haiming writes a personal instruction for the practitioner Xizhi. He sets the warning that the word 'knowing' opens many troubles beside the opposite saying that it opens many wonders, then refuses to let either maxim settle the question. He compares the character to a potent pill, invokes the Lotus Sutra's difficult wisdom, and asks what a Buddha actually knows. Poshan is the present author; his point is to test the student's wish to quiet knowing without turning it into a dead blank.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB185.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Fushi. Fushi Tongxian poses a puzzle to his assembly: a mother has seven children, six fail to meet a knowing friend, and the seventh is thrown into water; if a knowing friend is met, why is even that one unnecessary? The assembly's answers do not fit, so Fushi gives the warning about 'knowing' as his own answer. Here the maxim interrupts an attempted conceptual solution to the puzzle; it is not a reply by the monks.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J27/J27nB193.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yinyuan. At a New Year's Eve instruction, Yinyuan Longqi teases his monks for spending the day composing verses while still owing their food money. He warns how hard it is to withdraw a word once it enters an official office, then voices both maxims: knowing can open the gate of troubles and the gate of wonders. Even a stance of not knowing can be a root of both; he urges the assembly to release both opposed positions before celebrating the new year.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J28/J28nB208.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Guxue Zhe. A monk asks Guxue Zhenzhe why someone who knows the principle that birth is unborn can still be carried through birth and death. Guxue answers with the warning that the word 'knowing' opens many troubles. In his ensuing address he points to blue waters, red mountains, bird calls and even afflictions as the listener's own field, then presses further questions. The maxim rebukes the monk's reliance on knowing a proposition; it is Guxue's immediate answer, not the monk's question.

After recalling the image of the moon in a deep blue pool, Tianshu Xingzhi asks his assembly what it means to know. Their answers do not fit. He voices the warning that the word 'knowing' opens many troubles, adds that not knowing would be better, then disperses the gathering and returns to his room. ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB177.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Poshan. Poshan Haiming writes a personal instruction for the practitioner Xizhi. He sets the warning that the word 'knowing' opens many troubles beside the opposite saying that it opens many wonders, then refuses to let either maxim settle the question. He compares the character to a potent pill, invokes the Lotus Sutra's difficult wisdom, and asks what a Buddha actually knows. Poshan is the present author; his point is to test the student's wish to quiet knowing without turning it into a dead blank.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB185.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Fushi. Fushi Tongxian poses a puzzle to his assembly: a mother has seven children, six fail to meet a knowing friend, and the seventh is thrown into water; if a knowing friend is met, why is even that one unnecessary? The assembly's answers do not fit, so Fushi gives the warning about 'knowing' as his own answer. Here the maxim interrupts an attempted conceptual solution to the puzzle; it is not a reply by the monks.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J27/J27nB193.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yinyuan. At a New Year's Eve instruction, Yinyuan Longqi teases his monks for spending the day composing verses while still owing their food money. He warns how hard it is to withdraw a word once it enters an official office, then voices both maxims: knowing can open the gate of troubles and the gate of wonders. Even a stance of not knowing can be a root of both; he urges the assembly to release both opposed positions before celebrating the new year.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J28/J28nB208.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Guxue Zhe. A monk asks Guxue Zhenzhe why someone who knows the principle that birth is unborn can still be carried through birth and death. Guxue answers with the warning that the word 'knowing' opens many troubles. In his ensuing address he points to blue waters, red mountains, bird calls and even afflictions as the listener's own field, then presses further questions. The maxim rebukes the monk's reliance on knowing a proposition; it is Guxue's immediate answer, not the monk's question.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J37/J37nB399.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Tianshuzhi of Helin. After recalling the image of the moon in a deep blue pool, Tianshu Xingzhi asks his assembly what it means to know. Their answers do not fit. He voices the warning that the word 'knowing' opens many troubles, adds that not knowing would be better, then disperses the gathering and returns to his room. The phrase is his pointed closing answer to a failed group exchange; his further 'better not know' belongs to this local turn.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J38/J38nB430.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Qibaifu of Yuquan. Qibai Defu raises the old exchange in which a monk asks Yangshan whether the dharma body can preach, Yangshan points to someone else and pushes out a pillow, and Guishan praises the move as using a sword's edge. ClaimAnchors.ClaimText: 知之一字，眾禍之門

Senses.Explanation: In these six recorded discourses the maxim warns against treating the word 'knowing' as a settled possession. Some masters put it beside an opposite maxim about wonders, while others use it to interrupt a monk's answer or an inherited case. Poshan Haiming writes a personal instruction for the practitioner Xizhi. He sets the warning that the word 'knowing' opens many troubles beside the opposite saying that it opens many wonders, then refuses to let either maxim settle the question. He compares the character to a potent pill, invokes the Lotus Sutra's difficult wisdom, and asks what a Buddha actually knows. Poshan is the present author; his point is to test the student's wish to quiet knowing without turning it into a dead blank. Fushi Tongxian poses a puzzle to his assembly: a mother has seven children, six fail to meet a knowing friend, and the seventh is thrown into water; if a knowing friend is met, why is even that one unnecessary? The assembly's answers do not fit, so Fushi gives the warning about 'knowing' as his own answer. Here the maxim interrupts an attempted conceptual solution to the puzzle; it is not a reply by the monks. At a New Year's Eve instruction, Yinyuan Longqi teases his monks for spending the day composing verses while still owing their food money. He warns how hard it is to withdraw a word once it enters an official office, then voices both maxims: knowing can open the gate of troubles and the gate of wonders. Even a stance of not knowing can be a root of both; he urges the assembly to release both opposed positions before celebrating the new year. A monk asks Guxue Zhenzhe why someone who knows the principle that birth is unborn can still be carried through birth and death. Guxue answers with the warning that the word 'knowing' opens many troubles. In his ensuing address he points to blue waters, red mountains, bird calls and even afflictions as the listener's own field, then presses further questions. The maxim rebukes the monk's reliance on knowing a proposition; it is Guxue's immediate answer, not the monk's question. After recalling the image of the moon in a deep blue pool, Tianshu Xingzhi asks his assembly what it means to know. Their answers do not fit. He voices the warning that the word 'knowing' opens many troubles, adds that not knowing would be better, then disperses the gathering and returns to his room. The phrase is his pointed closing answer to a failed group exchange; his further 'better not know' belongs to this local turn. Qibai Defu raises the old exchange in which a monk asks Yangshan whether the dharma body can preach, Yangshan points to someone else and pushes out a pillow, and Guishan praises the move as using a sword's edge. Qibai says the teaching had already circulated before anyone spoke and calls the pillow move futile labor; he then asks the assembly if they understand and closes with the warning about knowing. The inherited case supplies the target, but the maxim is Qibai's present comment.

Occurrences.Kwic: 燄，嬾拈向上鉗鎚，撥置作家爐扇。鈍鐵頑銅任伊，璞玉渾金不羨，聊將萬象森羅，活把虛空烹煉。不許月白風清，那愛轟雷掣電？直得大地通紅，凡聖都盧不見，十虛無欠無餘，渾似金剛寶劍。假饒鋒利如斯，猶要重鎚百遍，更得分身出身，好與羅山相見。然雖如是，要見羅山則得，要見神鼎還隔一線好。諸禪德！且道是那一線？若也薦，直下翻身，推開手面；若不薦，一任九十日內橫拖倒拽，牽驢入阱。少間劉居士設齋，且去隨例嚥，要山僧說，也待來年正月半。」鄒深實為僧，請示眾。「知幻即離，不作方便；離幻即覺，亦無漸次。摩霄俊鷂，便合乘時；止濼困魚，徒勞激浪。不見昔日李都尉訪谷隱聰，問出家事，聰即舉：『崔趙公問徑山欽：「弟子出得家否？」欽云：「出家乃大丈夫事，非將相之所能為。」都尉便於此放卻身命，裂破鼻孔，遂云：「學道須是鐵漢，著手心頭便判，直取無上菩提，一切是非莫管。」如斯標致，差較些子。』所以道：出群須是英靈漢，敵勝還他獅子兒。你看他是箇血性漢子，直下便乃一刀兩段，佛也不奈他何，說什麼蘊魔、煩惱魔、生死魔？若待披忍辱鎧、操智慧刀、運上品心、發殊勝

Senses.Explanation: Know the kindness, repay the kindness. Hongzhi Zhengjue, raising the old Yunyan portrait-hanging exchange — Dongshan asked whether the one who said just-this still knows there is; if he did not know, how could he say it, and if he did, how would he consent to — appraises the old woman's heart as rearing a child and the monk's method as seizing the father's machine: know the kindness, repay the kindness — the phrase turns in the sentence, half consent half refusal, extra-measure prompting, and that is Dongshan's own. Dahui Zonggao, at the emperor's birthday hall, bows to the one who delivers all worlds — the golden wheel ruling the four continents, granting all beings peace — then demands: is there one who knows the kindness and repays it? and after a long silence answers with the calendar: of the year's three hundred sixty days, today alone is most auspicious. Yuanwu Keqin, blessing the sovereign — the whole earth receiving grace, dust-motes and lands all emitting the great treasure light — closes the hall on the formula: the one line of knowing-and-repaying, how does it go? No spirit fathoms the doing-of-nothing; everywhere the five-petaled flower fully opens. Tiantong Rujing, at the winter enlightenment-day, retells the six lost years, the eye lost beyond finding, the liar barely claiming the star — then rules that Cizhou Fangnian's praise of it is precisely what deserves the name know-the-kindness-repay-the-kindness, and if not, then a yearly bowl of tea on the eighth, with bows and incense, only dulls him. Wuyi Yuanlai, on the Buddha's birthday, lines up the birth, the seven steps, the one hand to heaven — already a defeat-mark — and Yunmen's declared one-stroke dog-feeding peace, calling it offering this deep heart to the dust-lands, just that named repaying the buddha's kindness, then demands of the assembly: is there one in this who knows the kindness and repays it? If so, come out and meet me; if not, while hands are strong and feet quick, settle this and stop being fooled by old monks' tongues. Jieweizhou Xingzhou, the same birthday elsewhere, asks who is the one who knows-and-repays, then rules that whoever resolves it draws the three-times buddhas and the successive patriarchs all to breathe through one nostril with him — no need for born-before-the-palace or taught-before-the-womb. Jifei Ruyi instructs his community that wearing the field-robe in this late age is no small karmic feat: remember the virtue and cultivate the virtue, know-and-repay, with penetrating birth-and-death as the one great matter — drop name and profit, and every drop of water and grain of rice is sweet; otherwise iron pellets and molten copper. And Yulin Tongxu, at the abbot's quarters of the repayment hall his donors built, names the radiant perfect fullness that everyone shades under, admits some have not yet known the kindness — the patrons and brothers now present are precisely the knowing-and-repaying ones, and must prove it at the tip of this monk's staff.

An unidentified monastic at Moshan says the line after Moshan Youqi challenges whether the questioner knows weight and measure. Yangshan Huiji uses it to interpret Linji's response to Huangbo. Baiyun Shouduan caps a contrast between immeasurable value and worthlessness with the line. Yinyuan Longqi gives it after an unidentified monastic's verse-like response during the release-of-retreat address. Across the cases, recognition and repayment form one conditional response.

Senses.Note: In his exchange with Zhaozhou, Nanquan says the way belongs neither to knowing nor to not knowing, then gives this pointed contrast. Tianran reads the encounter's opening and close together; Linye challenges the present assembly with it. Miyin insists on a living judgment, and Zhufeng rejects resting in Nanquan's explanation before supplying a new answer. These are distinct current responses to the quoted line.

Occurrences.Kwic: 頭頭爾、法法爾，如天普蓋、似地普擎，見聞覺知何曾有一毫頭假借？所謂：『只此見聞非見聞，更無聲色可呈君。箇中若了渾無事，體用何妨分不分？』具分也，落霞與孤鶩齊飛；不分也，野水共長天一色。到者裏，釋迦未降皇宮，還有佛法也無？達磨不來東土，喚他作不為人，得麼？龍淵今日不惜眉毛，已為諸人註破。還委悉麼？」良久，擲拂，云：「而今四海明如鏡，行人莫與路為讎。」卓杖，下座。南門眾居士預祝設齋請上堂師拈香畢，問答不錄，乃云：「趙州七百二十甲子已過去，龍淵三百六十甲子方到來，過去到來，兩彩一賽，娘娘依舊是婆婆，生平有甚不慶快？山僧住席以來，抱貧守拙，於人事荒疏，慚愧猶甚。今值暮景餘年，極承眾居士營齋，光臨法會，然信施難消，不妨為成道業。大眾！起心受食，淨名早訶；不起於心，食作麼受？離此二途，還有商量也無？昔南泉因趙州問：『如何是道？』泉曰：『平常心是道。』曰：『還可趣向也無？』泉曰：『擬向即乖』。曰：『不擬爭知是道？』泉曰：『道不屬知，不屬不知，知是妄覺，不知是無記。若真達不疑之道，猶如太虛廓然蕩豁，豈可強是非耶？』州於言下悟理。南師口頭水漉漉地，到這裡不無拗曲作直，趙州得便宜處失便宜，未免鈍置一上。今日龍淵與麼批判，設有傍不甘的出來問：『如何是道？』山僧劈脊便棒。何故？不惟解粘去縛，也使他知些痛癢始得。且道在山僧一句又作麼生？」師遂合掌云：「端坐受供養，施主常安樂。」一日，因老和尚顧院，到方丈見觀音像，問師云：「是什麼像？」師答：「送子觀音，祈求必應。」尚云：「終日與人祈，何不自求一個？」師云：「但求的不是子。」尚云：「恁麼也須著力。」師隨撾鼓示眾：「山僧於斯末後有語未進，仰勞大眾著語看。若確，有柄住山斧子兩手分付；如未能，且照顧始得。」師良久，云：「以眾為心賴得人，叢林相應始安寧。山僧縱有偷天手，孤掌從來不浪嗚。所以，插標建剎，庶子一上神通；即心即佛，馬祖通身泥水。衲僧家，竿木隨身，逢場不妨作戲；鉤錐在手，遇緣便可即宗。適蒙老漢垂勵，深知罪咎。」驀取拂豎，云：「須知鈍貨搶行，也要大家委悉。山僧恁麼舉揚，有伶俐衲僧便和聲放下，向者裡來，魔佛冤親互相策勵，不唧溜漢望岩而退，去住三家村裡，保頭也做不得一個。何故？斯事希有。世、出世間，有力者自能擔荷；為眾、為己，過量人便乃承當。所以，泰山

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 之終之，使無剩義而已。學人先為己地，亦不過在道法上既窺其體，直窮其用，使無空解而已。古人云：『有頭無尾時如何，終是不貴。有尾無頭時如何，雖飽無力。頭正尾正時如何，兒孫得力，室內不知。』人止知有尾無頭之為無力，而不知有頭無尾之為不貴，遂使理則甚明，情終難遣，乃自解云：一切法不可得，一切心不可得。夫法不可得、心不可得，盡天下人莫不皆然，幻因猶在，幻果難逃。古人云：何不道拽而不拽？固昭昭可鑒也。且舍頭亦無所謂尾，麻三觔、乾矢橛，此頭之極正者也。道則如是，前後若何？所以云：句前句後，正是學人難處，大法不明。正恁麼時，猶有趨向，劍去久矣，君方刻舟。不見趙州作沙彌時參見南泉，泉云：『有主沙彌？無主沙彌？』州云：『有主。』泉云：『主在什麼處？』州近前鞠躬云：『孟春猶寒，伏惟和尚尊候萬福。』明日陞座，州便出眾云：『如何是道？』泉云：『平常心是道。』州云：『還假趨向也無？』泉云：『擬向即乖。』州云：『不擬向爭知是道？』泉云：『道不屬知，不屬不知，知是妄覺，不知是無記。汝若深達不疑之道，猶如太虛廓然無礙，豈可強是非耶？』此趙州得體明用一箇大榜樣，已解道孟春猶寒，而復問云：『還假趨向也無？』此真得底人自審去就。大眾！不假趨向，頭一句如是，尾一句作麼生？莫是隨緣消舊業，更莫惹新災麼？且道箇裏還有差別也無？試細細諦當著。古人有因問云：『和尚手裏是箇什麼？』便舉拄杖云：『老僧年邁，離伊一步不得。』大眾！作麼生說箇不離底道理？莫便云：者箇還離得麼？且喜沒交涉。大凡衲僧家體究言句，須有來由。於今人都是沒來由底取次批判，明眼人笑汝。在昔達磨大師望神州有大乘氣航海而來，流通箇事，掃除階級，祇要汝特地承當，頭正尾正，不是但有其說。二祖安心已竟，一日復云：『外息諸緣，內心無喘，心如牆壁，可以入道。』二祖由是七年，乃有語云：『我已息諸緣。』磨云：『莫成斷滅否？』二祖云：『不成斷滅。』大眾！此不成斷滅，正是吾宗門頭一箇嫡真血脈。後來讓禪師聞馬祖開堂，密遣人往，纔見陞座，便出云：『作麼生？』馬祖云：『自從胡亂後，三十年不少鹽醬。』大眾！作麼生是馬大師不少鹽醬處？也須知是箇血脈。藥山在馬祖處悟得石頭禪，一日在石上坐次，石頭云：『子在此作什麼？』山云：『一物也不為。』頭云：『恁麼則閒坐也。』山云：『若閒坐即為也。』大

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 古人。雖則打草驚蛇，其實看孔著楔。汝等諸人要識二老即易，要識山僧則難。何故？」驀拈拄杖，云：「棒頭有眼明如日，要識真金火裏看。」示眾。「日來諸人不倦參請，只是往往錯過山僧棒頭。不惟不知錯過處，而返生多種狂解，道：『者棒如大火聚，四面不能入，擬之則燎卻面門。』又道：『者棒如金剛王寶劍，截斷聖凡情。不落有無見，破除生死窠窟，迥脫羅籠之表。』如斯狂解，深屈山僧棒頭。汝等諸人要識山僧棒頭麼？」驀拈拄杖，云：「莫將閒學解，埋沒祖師心。」示眾。「諸佛諸祖頂𩕳門，一一棒頭俱漏泄。若作佛法會，知君猶未瞥。不作佛法會，眼中已著屑。畢竟如何？」驀拈拄杖，卓一卓，云：「不別，不別。適纔有僧問棒頭下事，山僧隨手下一探竿，切恐諸人錯會。若道知痛痒底是，正是喚奴作郎，認賊為子。若道不知痛痒，人非土木，安得不知？不見趙州問南泉：『如何是道？』泉云：『平常心是道。』州云：『還假趣向也無？』泉云：『擬向即乖。』州云：『不擬怎知是道？』泉云：『道不屬知，不屬不知。知是妄覺，不知是無記。若真達不疑之道，猶若太虛廓然蕩豁，豈可強是非耶？』即今還有不落是非底麼？試出眾道看。」時有僧纔出，師云：「我不敢輕於汝等，汝等皆當作佛。」示眾。「昔日釋迦老子道：『知見立知，即無明本。知見無見，斯即涅槃。』」乃舉起拄杖，云：「這是拄杖子，諸人共知共見。且作麼生是知見無見底道理？」遂靠拄杖，云：「莫待是非來入耳，從前知己返為讎。」示眾。舉：「趙州道：『至道無難，唯嫌揀擇。但莫憎愛，洞然明白。』又道：『老僧不在明白裏，汝等諸人還護惜也無？』趙州老漢恁麼舉揚，可謂寸刃不施，皇化已遍。雖則騰身閫外，要且躲避無門。汝等諸人要識趙州老漢麼？也秪是個觀音院裏燒牛糞底老和尚。」示眾。「從上老宿，大有韜略。能擒能縱，能殺能活。山僧雖無如是伎能，單單秪善解黏去縛。解卻黏，釋卻縛，珍重諸君休咬嚼。適纔惟德禪人進方丈，問棒下意旨如何。山僧答：『一棒一條痕，一握一掌血。』德罔措。山僧云：『擬議即不得。』德猶問：『畢竟意旨如何？』山僧云：『猶要打在。』德禮拜而出。即今惟德可在這裡麼？」德便出眾。師云：「汝若作打會，入地獄如箭射。」德云：「畢竟意旨如何？」師云：「被子一問，瓦解冰消。」德便禮拜。師云：「汝是何道理便禮拜？」德擬議，師驀頭一棒，歸方丈。示

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 頭頭爾、法法爾，如天普蓋、似地普擎，見聞覺知何曾有一毫頭假借？所謂：『只此見聞非見聞，更無聲色可呈君。箇中若了渾無事，體用何妨分不分？』具分也，落霞與孤鶩齊飛；不分也，野水共長天一色。到者裏，釋迦未降皇宮，還有佛法也無？達磨不來東土，喚他作不為人，得麼？龍淵今日不惜眉毛，已為諸人註破。還委悉麼？」良久，擲拂，云：「而今四海明如鏡，行人莫與路為讎。」卓杖，下座。南門眾居士預祝設齋請上堂師拈香畢，問答不錄，乃云：「趙州七百二十甲子已過去，龍淵三百六十甲子方到來，過去到來，兩彩一賽，娘娘依舊是婆婆，生平有甚不慶快？山僧住席以來，抱貧守拙，於人事荒疏，慚愧猶甚。今值暮景餘年，極承眾居士營齋，光臨法會，然信施難消，不妨為成道業。大眾！起心受食，淨名早訶；不起於心，食作麼受？離此二途，還有商量也無？昔南泉因趙州問：『如何是道？』泉曰：『平常心是道。』曰：『還可趣向也無？』泉曰：『擬向即乖』。曰：『不擬爭知是道？』泉曰：『道不屬知，不屬不知，知是妄覺，不知是無記。若真達不疑之道，猶如太虛廓然蕩豁，豈可強是非耶？』州於言下悟理。南師口頭水漉漉地，到這裡不無拗曲作直，趙州得便宜處失便宜，未免鈍置一上。今日龍淵與麼批判，設有傍不甘的出來問：『如何是道？』山僧劈脊便棒。何故？不惟解粘去縛，也使他知些痛癢始得。且道在山僧一句又作麼生？」師遂合掌云：「端坐受供養，施主常安樂。」一日，因老和尚顧院，到方丈見觀音像，問師云：「是什麼像？」師答：「送子觀音，祈求必應。」尚云：「終日與人祈，何不自求一個？」師云：「但求的不是子。」尚云：「恁麼也須著力。」師隨撾鼓示眾：「山僧於斯末後有語未進，仰勞大眾著語看。若確，有柄住山斧子兩手分付；如未能，且照顧始得。」師良久，云：「以眾為心賴得人，叢林相應始安寧。山僧縱有偷天手，孤掌從來不浪嗚。所以，插標建剎，庶子一上神通；即心即佛，馬祖通身泥水。衲僧家，竿木隨身，逢場不妨作戲；鉤錐在手，遇緣便可即宗。適蒙老漢垂勵，深知罪咎。」驀取拂豎，云：「須知鈍貨搶行，也要大家委悉。山僧恁麼舉揚，有伶俐衲僧便和聲放下，向者裡來，魔佛冤親互相策勵，不唧溜漢望岩而退，去住三家村裡，保頭也做不得一個。何故？斯事希有。世、出世間，有力者自能擔荷；為眾、為己，過量人便乃承當。所以，泰山

Senses.Explanation: A root acknowledgment that the great matter is there, graded against what a speaker still owes or already owns. Juelang Daosheng grants the assembly the whole ten directions and still demands that they know there is the upward whole-lift, Yongjue Yuanxian's lantern-night verse gives the acknowledgment to badgers and calves while the buddhas of the three times get caught and beaten, Danxia Tianran's quoted couplet makes the acknowledgment arrive the moment intent is lifted, Xuedou Chongxian denies it of the old foreigner who missed the one penetration, and Wuyi Yuanlai prescribes the doubt-mass that stops knowing there is a flesh-and-blood body and mind. Hongzhi Zhengjue returns a monk's exchange with the ruling that he must still know there is the turning-around road, Yuanwu Keqin ties seeing the whole-lift and half-lift to those who know there is, Caoshan Benji answers Yunmen that the secret place is exactly why one does not know there is, Dahui Zonggao credits a soldier who knows there is a true teacher and trusts the affair, and Liao'an Qingyu warns that even a faultless world is only a turning word and one must know there is the season of the whole lift.

Senses.Explanation: A person who knows there is this is someone whom the record presents as recognizing the matter at hand and acting from that recognition. Zhe’an Jingfan says such a person turns with circumstances and uses things without a fixed pattern. Fachang Yiyu says such a person enters a forest without moving the grass and enters water without moving a wave. Yuanwu Keqin says such a person can communicate openly when the right person is present, while Hansong Zhicao says one move is enough to know where the matter lands.

Senses.Note: Shenzang’s line says that knowing without fixed knowing is different from a mere lack of knowledge. Miyun opens a sermon with it and unfolds knowing and not knowing through ordinary and sage; Wuyi quotes Shenzang among competing teachings on knowledge and annotates each clause; Yun’e tests the Shenzang, Nanquan, and Huangbo exchange with his own sharp comment; Dayu voices the line before contrasting two teachers and challenging his audience. Each turn gives the apparent paradox a separate use.

Senses.Explanation: “Knowing without fixed knowing” describes a live knowing that cannot be confused with ignorance. Miyun unfolds knowing and not knowing through ordinary and sage, while Wuyi quotes Shenzang among older voices and annotates the line clause by clause. Yun’e critiques the Shenzang, Nanquan, and Huangbo exchange; Dayu voices the line and tests his listeners with it.

Senses.PreferredTarget: When knowing and seeing set up another knowing, that is the root of ignorance
AlternateTargets: To establish a knowing upon knowing and seeing is where ignorance begins
SearchAliases: knowing seeing establish knowing root of ignorance
Senses.Note: The scripture says that imposing another knowing on knowing and seeing is the root of ignorance. Liangting and Hanyue explain the danger of turning awareness into an object. Yezhu and Yanxi challenge inherited ways of punctuating or using the line. Huitang responds to the text with an immediate account of seeing, while Chushi asks his assembly how far the paired terms are from one another. Their uses turn a scriptural sentence into an active test of reading and seeing.

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 一簡點，一覺照，即傷他觸他。弟子于此一事，已信得十分，決無岐嚮矣。此便是躋實地人之初步也。大道最忌奇特玄妙，奇玄正是兩頭心。古人不過大巧若拙，大拙若巧而已。故巧人多鏤木為篆，拙人常抱枯樁，不知渾金樸玉，聲價自重。大都日用應緣，只用機先，一向隨事了事，不要管他。若是撥著頭角，便與一刀兩段，不可放過。答趙文度郡伯答趙文度郡伯前者山中數日，相對殷勤譚一大事，非有力大人，豈能湥求力究如此？居士夙具殊勝種子，從今觸雨生發，不可遏捺，真不易得也。承諭《宗鏡錄》言三途無分別而不發業，故不受報等語，簡之具在七十四卷第四十葉。大都俱生二字，教中雖細解註，終不明言，故知教之人多不得力。須知本明與無明元是一箇，明極故不覺，不覺則不守自性，不守故任運起惑，起惑則生明造業。所以眾生流浪生死，皆因無明與本明俱生，俱生則業相動而轉相向外，便現出現行，行現即智相生而分別起矣。所以要出生死，先斷聰明，聰明通身是分別，故總別俱報，謂之定業，斷不能避。《楞嚴》云：「知見立知，即無明本，知見無見，斯即涅槃。」此兩句便該括盡矣。只是今人於知見處不能無見，苦無下手處，如人說食終不能飽耳。今日參禪，正為下手方便，若一得之，便終日行而不現行，終日分別而非煩惱分別，惑尚不起，何況造業受報耶？現行是明白底，明白便能作主宰。《宗鏡》亦曰：「主宰是任持義，即我相根本主宰是第七識，恒恒執我不肯打失，打失即任運矣。」禪者任運而且斷惑業三途，惑業太重俱生強盛而亦任運，以任運迷極故不受總報，別報是偶爾成文。喻如癡人隨主人驅率便打殺人，罪當坐主，以僕癡極無知不坐殺罪，不過是牽連耳。大力鬼打舍利弗，而舍利弗是果上人，其緣勝故入地獄；鸚鵡聞法，以法力勝故生天北；俱盧洲因修癡福故感癡報，謂之生長壽天，是八難之一，此洲癡人亦不受報。大概此輩癡極故無分別，禪者透過明白故無分別，故大悟底人卻翻迷了，此非迷悟之迷，乃與佛同體無記之迷，即所謂知見無見者也。今要參禪，先將平生知見明白抹過一邊，將去不得底話頭橫看豎看、轉看轉迷悶，迷悶不過，于計較不得處忽地一迸，便會知見無見底方便，終日任運與佛無二矣。草草贅語，聊為宗鏡作箇註腳，居士高明自當朗鑑。答王聞修廉憲答王聞修廉憲二年不接清範，想居士珍重杜門，必湥進此道。得手札，知努力大事，務在必證真人為道，自

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 。師曰：舉則易，見還難。彌盧頂上天風寒，峩峩直下蒼龍窟。誰敢覰著？舉僧問雲門：如何是正法眼？門曰：普。師曰：更道箇瞎，且圖兩得相見。舉疎山問僧：曾到雪峰否？僧曰：曾到。山曰：我已前到彼，是事不足，如今作麼生？僧曰：如今足也。山曰：粥足？飯足？僧無對。雲門代曰：粥足，飯足。師曰：是則是，要且無佛法道理。僧問：如何無佛法道理？師却問僧：是爾尋常將什麼喫粥喫飯？僧曰：將口喫。師喝曰：露柱為什麼却飽？你若嚼破一粒米，山河大地欺你去。舉：雲門大師拈拄杖示眾曰：拄杖子化為龍，吞却乾坤了也。山河大地，甚處得來？師曰：明眼宗師，至今猶在。忽若有箇漢出來道：者箇是拄杖子，山河大地有甚過？也許伊具一隻眼。舉德山一日訪龍潭曰：久嚮龍潭，及乎到來，潭又不見，龍又不現。潭曰：子親到龍潭。雪竇曰：將錯就錯。師曰：雪竇與麼道，不知德山將錯就錯，不知龍潭將錯就錯。識休咎底衲僧，必知去處。未過關者，亦宜辨白。還相委悉麼？縱饒栽種得，不是棟梁材。舉教中道：是故汝今知見立知，即無明本。知見無見，斯即涅槃無漏真淨。云何是中更容他物？師曰：盡乾坤大地，皆是上座眼睛，更無纖毫隔礙。只如今見但見，聞但聞，行但行，坐但坐，總不動著。爾若動著，我即朝到西天，暮歸東土。舉先聖道：生死與菩提，二定真有法。於此若生疑，聾瞽無慧眼。又道：生死與菩提，二定非有法。於此若生疑，聾瞽無慧眼。師曰：為復一般，為是相違，為當別有道理，試斷看。舉雲門大師一日問僧：從甚處來？僧曰：江西來。門曰：踏破多少草鞋？其僧不對。師曰：雲門大師已是張虎豹之紋，又不覺落在者僧陷穽。而今還有扶起雲門底漢，道取一轉語，却與黃龍相見。敢問此語作麼生道？舉寒山道：我聞釋迦佛，不知在何方。思量得去處，不離我道場。師曰：是什麼思量？釋迦老子在甚處？試定當看。舉同光帝一日與興化坐次，帝問：寡人收得中原一寶，只是無人酬價。化曰：試借陛下寶看。帝乃舒開幞頭脚。化曰：君王之寶，誰敢酬價？師曰：興化雖則一期見機而作，爭奈埋沒他一朝天子。當時若作興化，但向伊道：蚌蛤之珍，收得也無用處。教他向後別有生涯，免見傍觀者哂。而今忽若有人問上座，又作麼生酬價？舉：僧問玄沙：三乘十二分教即不要，如何是祖師西來意？沙曰：三乘十二分教總不要。師曰：如珠在淵，本自無纇。如玉在石，本自無瑕。識

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 去，要住便住，誰障得你？誰礙得你？豈不俊哉？豈不快哉？且道生死路頭作麼生撥？空手把鉏頭，步行騎水牛，人從橋上過，橋流水不流。若不會，與你下箇註脚：空手把鉏頭，驟馬上高樓，步行騎水牛，閙處冷湫湫。人從橋上過，飯籮頭受餓，橋流水不流，撥火覔浮漚。時不待人參。復舉：圓覺經云：居一切時不起妄念，於諸妄心亦不息滅，住妄想境不加了知，於無了知不辨真實。師云：若然者，道有也得、道無也得，向上也得、向下也得，得也得、不得也得，數片白雲籠古寺，一條綠水繞青山。上堂。羣芳已謝，百穀云滋，綠樹鶯啼，雕梁燕語。大野涼風颯颯，長天細雨濛濛，惟一堅密身，一切塵中現。還有不現的時節麼？卓拄杖一下。上堂：鷹化為鳩眼在，魚化為龍鱗在，凡化為聖心在。阿那箇是你心？喝一喝。上堂。天不能葢，誰是能葢者？地不能載，誰是能載者？日月不能照，誰是能照者？父母不能生，誰是能生者？這一句子亦能迷却天下人，亦能悟却天下人。豎拂子，云：開眼也著，合眼也著。擲拂子，云：是什麼？上堂：知見立知，即無明本。知見無見，斯即涅槃。無明涅槃，相去多少？良久：行到水窮處，坐看雲起時。上堂：宗門中瓶中鵝喻，井中人喻，󰈧中山喻，教乘中水中月喻，鏡中像喻，庫中刀喻，鼎中金喻，瓶中空喻。諸有智者，要以譬喻而得開解。三十年後悟去，不得孤負老僧。久雨不晴，劄。上堂：太陽溢目，萬里不挂片雲。古人道，青天也須喫棒。空將未歸意，說與欲行人。上堂。舉手云：開即成掌，五指參差。在臨濟則三要三玄，在洞山則正偏回互，在雲門則三句擡薦，在溈仰則父子唱酬，在法眼則唯心唯識。禪門五派，有卷有舒。乃握拳云：如今為拳，必無高下。既無高下，坐斷古今。拈燈籠向佛殿裏，將三門來燈籠上。上堂。半夜子心住，無生即生死。拈拄杖，云：這箇不是無生。卓一下，云：生死向什麼處去也？昨夜三更，在方丈內偶然踏著一物，不知是瓦、不知是石，天曉看來，元是一顆爛桃。一疑是瓦也不是、一疑是石也不是，天曉看來是爛桃，祇這疑心何處起？亦無神、亦無鬼，子細思量祇是你。昔日，玄沙同僧入山見虎，僧云：和尚，虎。沙云：是你，虎。乃撫掌三下，下座。解夏，小參。僧問：佛佛授手，祖祖相傳，未審是授衣耶？傳法耶？學人上來，請師指示。師云：黃河九曲。進云：昔日大慧和尚居洋嶼菴，一夏打發一十三人，畢竟是有傳授？無傳授？師

Senses.Explanation: The paired clause locates ignorance in a knowing added to knowing and seeing. Liangting and Hanyue explain the scriptural distinction; Huitang gives a direct response to the quoted text. Yezhu, Yanxi, and Chushi turn the wording into fresh questions about reading and seeing in the hall.

Entries.SourceTerm: 知見立知，即無明本。知見無見，斯即涅槃

Senses.PreferredTarget: To add knowing to what is seen is the root of ignorance. To see without fixing a view is nirvana.
AlternateTargets: Turning seeing into a fixed knowing begins ignorance; seeing without that added view is nirvana.
SearchAliases: Knowing added to seeing is ignorance seeing without view is nirvana
Senses.Note: The Surangama pair first warns that adding a fixed knowing to seeing is ignorance, then names seeing without that added view as nirvana. Linye quotes it and raises a staff to ask what such seeing is. Tianran argues that even grasping the scriptural point may fall short in a Chan encounter. Chushi asks how far ignorance and nirvana are apart, while Yu'an asks whether they are one or two. The sources present the exact words as inherited scripture; the four masters' later questions are their own.

Occurrences.Kwic: 擔云：「楖栗橫挑不顧人，直入千峰萬峰去。」須是與麼始得。若到與麼田地，渠且不是與麼人。何故？生平用盡心力，祇圖識得者些好惡。臨濟大師云：「大凡舉唱宗乘，須一句中具三玄三要始得。」古人立法將以防偽，誰知後世反滋傳偽，病在不求者一句端的著落，卻去辨別甚麼是玄？甚麼是要？如此豈不是傳偽？又有云：「祇如庭前柏樹子、麻三斤、乾矢橛者，便是那一句了。」如此豈不是傳偽？不見德山云：「但參活句，莫參死句。」若是死句下薦得，千生萬劫沒你出頭分。所以汾陽深明斯旨，乃頌云：「三玄三要事難分，得意忘言道易親。一句明明該萬象，重陽九月菊花新。」分明向道：得意忘言道易親，區區髑髏邊覓甚麼汁？你若觸著便省，不妨轉死為活，便無許多藥忌，便見古人立言之旨。以此供養三世諸佛，亦何愧歟？談宗家，往往開大口抹殺教乘。殊不知渠實落做處，尚不能及教乘極則。祇如《楞嚴》云：「根塵同源，縛脫無二。識性虛妄，猶若空華。」又云：「由塵發知，因根有相。相見無性，同於交蘆。」又云：「知見立知，即無明本。知見無見，斯即涅槃。」今時人果能與麼會得到得者田地麼？直教會得到得，尚未是宗門下事，況猶在依稀間耶？余嘗向人道：「達磨未渡江，如清涼、寶誌公諸聖賢，亦曾闡化一代。書冊所載清涼心王銘、寶誌公大乘十讚、四料簡、十二時歌，未嘗不道盡，為何初祖復來？」故知他大有長處。所以世尊四十九年說法度生，臨末梢頭，方纔拈青蓮花，目顧人天云：「吾有涅槃妙心，教外別傳，付與摩訶迦葉。」正是此意。後來祖師亦云：「三乘十二分教，何曾露者箇消息？」趙州亦云：「我尋常祇是以本分事接人，若要隨根上下，自有三乘十二分教在。」他時遇明眼人，亦不道老僧辜負伊。于今末法，將來為宗師底痾淥淥地，恨不得學人會去，趁門庭熱鬧。殊不知儘他說得傳得，尚不是教乘極則，更要學人會箇甚麼？且何故知他不是教乘極則？為他教乘極則，亦須有箇悟處。既悟得，又復行得。所以世尊在世時，凡依教修行，各各皆有所證，不徒解了便休。于今宗師痾淥淥地，且不管學人悟不悟、行不行，祇要他會，早晚叫入方丈，低聲細語，道甚麼是今時，甚麼是劫外，如何是得體，如何是得用，者樣便是獨脫一路，那樣便是結果收因。學人不知，以為宗門事祇是如此，一任橫說豎說，且莫道把學人悟門一塞塞斷，就是恁麼說底傳底，謂與達磨西來之旨有分毫交涉否？須知此事大

Occurrences.Kwic: 去，要住便住，誰障得你？誰礙得你？豈不俊哉？豈不快哉？且道生死路頭作麼生撥？空手把鉏頭，步行騎水牛，人從橋上過，橋流水不流。若不會，與你下箇註脚：空手把鉏頭，驟馬上高樓，步行騎水牛，閙處冷湫湫。人從橋上過，飯籮頭受餓，橋流水不流，撥火覔浮漚。時不待人參。復舉：圓覺經云：居一切時不起妄念，於諸妄心亦不息滅，住妄想境不加了知，於無了知不辨真實。師云：若然者，道有也得、道無也得，向上也得、向下也得，得也得、不得也得，數片白雲籠古寺，一條綠水繞青山。上堂。羣芳已謝，百穀云滋，綠樹鶯啼，雕梁燕語。大野涼風颯颯，長天細雨濛濛，惟一堅密身，一切塵中現。還有不現的時節麼？卓拄杖一下。上堂：鷹化為鳩眼在，魚化為龍鱗在，凡化為聖心在。阿那箇是你心？喝一喝。上堂。天不能葢，誰是能葢者？地不能載，誰是能載者？日月不能照，誰是能照者？父母不能生，誰是能生者？這一句子亦能迷却天下人，亦能悟却天下人。豎拂子，云：開眼也著，合眼也著。擲拂子，云：是什麼？上堂：知見立知，即無明本。知見無見，斯即涅槃。無明涅槃，相去多少？良久：行到水窮處，坐看雲起時。上堂：宗門中瓶中鵝喻，井中人喻，󰈧中山喻，教乘中水中月喻，鏡中像喻，庫中刀喻，鼎中金喻，瓶中空喻。諸有智者，要以譬喻而得開解。三十年後悟去，不得孤負老僧。久雨不晴，劄。上堂：太陽溢目，萬里不挂片雲。古人道，青天也須喫棒。空將未歸意，說與欲行人。上堂。舉手云：開即成掌，五指參差。在臨濟則三要三玄，在洞山則正偏回互，在雲門則三句擡薦，在溈仰則父子唱酬，在法眼則唯心唯識。禪門五派，有卷有舒。乃握拳云：如今為拳，必無高下。既無高下，坐斷古今。拈燈籠向佛殿裏，將三門來燈籠上。上堂。半夜子心住，無生即生死。拈拄杖，云：這箇不是無生。卓一下，云：生死向什麼處去也？昨夜三更，在方丈內偶然踏著一物，不知是瓦、不知是石，天曉看來，元是一顆爛桃。一疑是瓦也不是、一疑是石也不是，天曉看來是爛桃，祇這疑心何處起？亦無神、亦無鬼，子細思量祇是你。昔日，玄沙同僧入山見虎，僧云：和尚，虎。沙云：是你，虎。乃撫掌三下，下座。解夏，小參。僧問：佛佛授手，祖祖相傳，未審是授衣耶？傳法耶？學人上來，請師指示。師云：黃河九曲。進云：昔日大慧和尚居洋嶼菴，一夏打發一十三人，畢竟是有傳授？無傳授？師云：斫額望扶桑。進云

Occurrences.Kwic: 舉似大眾：非圖邁古超今，且要應時應節。九日無白醪，萸茶滿椀澆；十日有黃菊，凉飈動林麓；五更鐘未鳴，過鴈兩三聲；更欲求玄旨，迢迢十萬程。上堂：金佛不度爐，木佛不度火，泥佛不度水，真佛屋裏坐趙州，眼光爍破四天下，未免錯認驢鞍槁作阿爺下頷。畢竟如何？覓佛不見佛，討祖不見祖，甜瓜徹蒂甜，苦瓠連根苦。上堂：譬如牛過窓櫺，頭角四蹄都過了，唯有尾巴過不得。且道誵訛在甚麼處？良久：虎咬大蟲，蛇吞鱉鼻。上堂，舉：趙州和尚道：老僧除二時上堂，粥飯是雜用心處。師云：趙州有年無德，錯下名言。燒香禮拜是雜用心，看經講教是雜用心，參禪學道是雜用心，了生達死是雜用心，成佛作祖是雜用心。唯二時上堂，粥飯是善用心。何也？不曾咬破一粒米。上堂，僧問：如何是毗盧師？師云：斷跟草鞋。進云：如何是法身主？師云：尖簷席帽。進云：學人不會。師云：見成行貨，有什麼不會？僧擬議，師便喝，乃云：春雨如膏，春風如刀，春光似箭，斷不相饒。卓拄杖。龍峯拄杖無遷變，又見鵝黃上柳條。上堂：知見立知，即無明本。知見無見，斯即涅槃。無明涅槃，是一是二？一夜落花雨，滿城流水香。上堂。十五日已前，覔甚文殊普賢？十五日已後，釋迦老子不知有。正當十五日，天上無彌勒，地下無彌勒。時有僧躍出問：天上無彌勒，地下無彌勒，未審誰與安名？師云：我行荒草裏，汝又入深村。解夏，上堂。四月十五日，結却布袋頭，十字縱橫底有甚數？七月十五日，解却布袋頭，無繩自縛底有甚數？喝！結也不可得，解亦何曾有？解結二圓離，面南看北斗。下座。上堂，僧問：至道無難，唯嫌揀擇。不揀擇時如何？師云：遇飯即飯，遇茶即茶。僧禮拜，師云：放汝三十棒。乃云：纔逢解夏，又見中秋，看看白盡少年頭。驀拈拄杖：旋嵐偃嶽而常靜，江河競注而不流，野馬飄鼓而不動，日月歷天而不周。卓拄杖：有時乘好月，不覺過滄洲。愚菴和尚語錄卷第二愚菴和尚語錄卷第三杭州路淨慈報恩禪寺語錄杭州路淨慈報恩禪寺語錄門人正除等編師於至正戊戌七月二十日，承行宣政院領院官太尉丞相達識帖穆爾，差宣使九曜奴馳驛於蘇州，受業海雲院，敦請入寺。據室云：刮龜毛於鐵牛背上，朝打三千；截兔角於石女腰邊，莫打八百。指東劃西，鼓唇搖舌，耳居門外，擊石火，閃電光，冰稜上度過九𨸰，劒刃上拾得全身，苕帚柄聊與三十。總不與麼來時如何？拈拄杖：吽！吽！指法座云：盡十方世界是普光
